adventure.title: The Concord of Aurelune
adventure.synopsis: The Shadowfell army that raised the Pall has been driven from Orison, but its siege-work now feeds itself. At moonrise after the seventh court day, it will close the last Fey road into the city. A paving stone carried from Orison remembers noon beneath Aurelune's Sunseed, proving the relic can restore the sky if it crosses in time. King Caelir III refuses the proposed loan. Seven of the ten Great Banners, with all four seasons represented, can compel joint custody for one named undertaking. Orison's petitioners must win those seals and make their rival bargains govern one exact instrument before the road closes.
adventure.premise: A defeated Shadowfell siege-work is closing around Orison. The Sunseed can restore the city's sky, but it must enter the Crown Passage before moonrise after the seventh court day. In Aurelune's high court, recognized speakers cannot knowingly lie; the adventurers must win seven seasonally balanced banners and draft one undertaking their incompatible truths can obey.
adventure.explanation: There is no concealed culprit or secret vote. The Pall, the Sunseed test, the deadline, the voting rule, the king's opposition, and the available settlements are public. Orison's Lantern Road compact guarantees an emergency audience and passage into Aurelune; it grants neither treaty equality nor command of the rescue. The adventure assumes only that Orison has commissioned the adventurers to petition and negotiate beside Envoy Mara Venn; their identities, history, internal offices, and preferred coalition remain open. The court is assembling a coalition, not filling offices. The Canopy turns its leaves toward recognized speakers; plaques change category when the court recognizes a relation; oath-mirrors retain abandoned promises; and banner seals attach only to exact text. No recognized speaker can knowingly assert what is false, so omission, narrowed answers, selective precedent, and arranged context remain political weapons. Play turns on making rival houses truthfully recognize one shared undertaking, then preserving enough room inside it for Orison and the Crown to act. Every bargain changes which banners can stand together when the Sunseed rises.

references.title: Theron Eiral
references.summary: The Lord Chamberlain must certify a lawful Concord while House Eiral's banner remains a separate political choice.
references.content:
## One robe, two rings

Theron Eiral is both Lord Chamberlain and House Eiral's court voice. He changes neither robe nor expression between those roles; at the Twilight Laurel he turns one ring when he crosses from the Chamberlain's black desk to the house table. Official service never counts as House Eiral's seal.

## What the black desk must certify

Theron reads the Concord of Open Hands, governs its calendar, and certifies only an instrument whose undertaking, custody, command, term, liability, recall, and return can operate together. He must identify a defect specifically. He may require a correction session or refuse inconsistent language, but he cannot turn political dislike into a legal defect.

## What the laurel table wants

At the laurel table, Theron wants a settlement the court can execute without spending the next decade pretending that humiliation was concord. House Eiral may seal while he warns of another defect, withhold its banner while he certifies, or support his service as chair without adding a vote.

references.title: The Sunseed
references.summary: A royal relic whose remembered daylight can restore Orison if its root-casket enters the Crown Passage before moonrise after Court Day Seven.
references.content:
## Dawn beneath the throne

The Sunseed burns inside a clear glass root beneath King Caelir III's throne and lays the same mild dawn across the Argent Canopy. A paving stone from Orison's noon market warms beneath it, sheds the Pall's black frost, and casts its former shadow. Aurelune's Dawnward keepers have repeated the test: the remedy is demonstrated, not speculative.

## The road closes before custody begins

The root-casket must enter the Crown Passage before moonrise after Court Day Seven, before the Pall closes the last road to its center. The custody term begins only when the Sunseed is uprooted, so the passage deadline and the negotiated loan term are different clocks.

## What uprooting places at risk

Uprooting the Sunseed thins the Dawnward and disturbs Aurelune's seasonal roads. Crown ownership can survive joint possession and purpose-limited use, but any valid instrument must preserve a royal interest and state exact custody, command, term, liability, recall, and return.

references.title: King Caelir III
references.summary: Aurelune's king guards the Sunseed, builds a genuine Crown-led rescue, and must honor any valid Concord he cannot prevent.
references.content:
## The trust beneath his throne

Caelir III is King of Aurelune and the Sunseed's royal guardian. He accepts that the relic can restore Orison's day. His opposition is to surrendering the trust, not to saving lives: uprooting the Sunseed weakens the Dawnward, disturbs the seasonal roads, and creates a precedent every neighboring realm may invoke.

## Six days under the Crown

Caelir can open royal gates and passages, commission officers, fund evacuation, file a Crown instrument, and commit the Crown to exact custody, command, liability, recall, and return duties. He prefers a six-day expedition under exclusive Crown custody and command, with evacuation and lesser relics as fallbacks. That plan is genuine relief and a political rival to Orison's petition.

## What seven banners can compel

Caelir cannot veto a valid Concord of Open Hands. Seven seasonally balanced Great Banners may compel joint custody once Theron certifies one coherent instrument that preserves a royal interest. Caelir may join after certification; his joinder improves cooperation but does not create validity. If compelled, he honors the text, interprets ambiguity in favor of the Crown and Aurelune, and withholds generosity rather than performance. The Oath of the Unbroken Word forbids knowing falsehood, not omission, narrow scope, or exact distinctions between rescue, custody, command, and consent.

references.title: Envoy Mara Venn
references.summary: Orison's civil envoy carries the emergency mandate, proves the Sunseed remedy, and guards the city's consent inside any rescue instrument.
references.content:
## A sealed commission and a black-frosted stone

Mara Venn is Orison's civil envoy beside the adventurers. She carries the surviving council's sealed emergency commission and brought the noon-market paving stone whose remembered warmth and shadow demonstrate that the Sunseed can restore Orison's day.

## What Orison may accept

Mara states what Orison will accept from allied custodians and commanders, speaks wherever the emergency mandate gives the city standing, and may accept or reject the undertaking named in the final instrument. She can require Orison's consent before the undertaking is redirected while leaving ordinary execution to an agreed commander. Her acceptance does not replace seven banner seals, grant treaty equality by itself, or define the adventurers' identities, offices, coalition, or route.

## The promise a changed word releases

Mara wants a rescue Orison can govern rather than relief that turns the city into a ward or places its civil authority under foreign command. She distrusts promises the besieged government cannot perform while much of it remains underground. Personal surety, fosterage, liability, and consultation bind her only through exact terms she accepts; none follows automatically from her office. At the drafting table she asks which promise a changed word has released.

references.title: Marshal Ysandre Serathiel
references.summary: House Serathiel's marshal turns compassion into a command problem and supports the Sunseed only through a coherent, supplied military structure.
references.content:
## Every mercy needs an order

Ysandre Serathiel is marshal of House Serathiel, the Noon Spear. She accepts that the Sunseed can save Orison and asks what compassion has not answered: who commands the route, protection, tempo, contingency, and return. She states military capacities precisely enough that listeners often supply the prediction she has not made. Her assumptions must be asked for as carefully as her conclusions.

## Route, guard, tempo, return

Ysandre can supply troops, transport, engineers, and expedition command. She may accept a royal officer, divided authority, or another commander when the structure remains operationally coherent. Expedition command does not by itself confer authority over Orison's civil government or Caldus Serevin's eastern marches, and House Serathiel's banner seal remains distinct from any command appointment.

## What she yields before command

Ysandre will not support an unguarded civilian custody arrangement with no effective command and no replacement defense for Aurelune. She can yield title, ceremony, and even personal command before she yields the existence of a command structure. The present commander, troop allocation, term, and border package remain matters for the petition and play.

references.title: Comptroller Mirelle Orelle
references.summary: House Orelle's comptroller makes every rescue cost name its bearer and separates genuine loss from capital and acquired advantage.
references.content:
## Loss, Capital, Advantage

Mirelle Orelle is comptroller of House Orelle, the Golden Sheaf. She prices the Sunseed undertaking through three public ledgers: Loss for what is consumed, Capital for assets that retain value, and Advantage for monopolies, access, ownership, and political reach acquired as compensation. Her totals are correct inside the categories she has chosen; the useful question is which category made the total possible.

## What her ledgers make executable

Mirelle can finance replacement wards, transport, reserves, insurance, and reconstruction, and can structure capped guarantees among several bearers. She can make material promises executable and auditable. She cannot make reusable Orelle property into an unrecoverable public loss by naming it so, bind Orison to privileges it has not accepted, or turn House Orelle's seal into the source of every financial function.

## Every bearer and benefit named

Mirelle will not accept unlimited Aurelune liability paired with complete immunity for Orison. She does accept shared risk, fault-based liability, returned reserves, ordinary contracts, and narrow compensation when each bearer and benefit is named. The current valuation, guarantors, collateral, privileges, and final bargain remain in the ledgers and petition.

references.title: Archivist-Lord Pelion Namaris
references.summary: Aurelune's archivist-lord tests the Sunseed petition against precedent, exact drafting, audit, and the rule a later hostile court might claim.
references.content:
## The later case waits in the index

Pelion Namaris is archivist-lord of House Namaris, the Amber Quill. He asks not only which precedent governs, but which later judgment limits it and which sentence an unfriendly court may quote a century later. The Oath permits him to select an accurate controlling passage without volunteering every distinction; asking for the limiting record is part of dealing with him.

## What the amber quills can separate

Pelion can retrieve precedent, expose drafting defects, define audit and review procedures, separate title from custody and use, and stabilize return, amendment, and sunset language. He can test whether associated covenants remain public, enforceable, and compatible with the central petition. He does not certify the Concord—that duty belongs to Theron Eiral—and his preferred precedent does not become law merely because he supplied it.

## Words that survive their authors

Pelion will not support operative language whose effect depends on goodwill after the vote. He accepts narrow emergency findings, relic-specific rules, later review, and carefully indexed side covenants. The current draft, cited authorities, audit appointments, and House Namaris seal remain changing court state.

references.title: Warden Caldus Serevin
references.summary: The warden of Aurelune's eastern marches demands a measurable defense and lawful response before the Sunseed weakens the Dawnward.
references.content:
## Needles against the old rings

Caldus Serevin is warden of House Serevin, the Silent Fir, and speaks for the eastern marches that become vulnerable when the Sunseed leaves. He reports observable movement and requires listeners to distinguish an invasion signal from the established seasonal baseline. His restraint of speech does not make every omitted comparison immaterial.

## What the eastern watch may command

Caldus can command forces lawfully assigned to the marches, evaluate the border, operate substitute defenses, and verify or recommend a response to a defined breach. Expedition command and border command are separate. He cannot recall the Sunseed merely because he fears an attack unless the final instrument grants him that authority and states its trigger, verification, and scope.

## A breach that can be measured

Caldus will not support a loan that leaves the marches without mitigation or any lawful response to an actual invasion. He can accept funded reserves, substitute wards, shorter exposure, or a multi-party objective trigger instead of unilateral recall. Current reports, deployments, commanders, thresholds, and recall powers remain in the court record and petition.

references.title: Orison
references.summary: The mortal city beneath the Pall is the endangered polity whose sky, civil agency, and political future the Concord may preserve or redefine.
references.content:
## A city under a failing sky

Orison is the city enclosed by the Pall. Its defenders drove away the Shadowfell host that began the siege-work, but much of the surviving government and population remains under a failing sky. The surviving council sealed an emergency commission authorizing its envoy and petitioners to seek the Sunseed; that commission does not predefine a fresh delegation's identities, offices, route, or coalition.

## Standing without wardship

The Lantern Road Compact secures Orison an emergency audience and access to a Crown Passage. It does not by itself make Orison Aurelune's treaty equal. Orison retains civil authority over its people and may accept or reject the undertaking and any redirection imposed in its name. Expedition command can govern the operation without governing the city, and protection does not make Orison a ward unless exact terms do so.

## Which city survives the rescue

Evacuating citizens, breaking the Pall, restoring natural day, preserving the city, and rebuilding its institutions are different undertakings. The Sunseed can restore Orison's sky, while collateral, trade privileges, fosterage, military authority, and public credit can determine what polity survives the rescue. Those choices belong to the active petition rather than this record.

references.title: The Ashen Bough
references.summary: House Avarre's vacant, unseasoned Great Banner may become a tenth vote only through a lawful judgment that preserves the distinct claims of Mirath Avarre and Aven Tal.
references.content:
## One empty chair, two true claims

The Ashen Bough is House Avarre's vacant Great Banner and counts for no season. Vaelor Avarre died childless by blood. His elder sister, Lady Mirath Avarre, is the nearest dynast and served three times as his military regent. Vaelor also executed a valid sealed adoption of the mortal-born Aven Tal, making Aven his child for household, estate, and personal obligations, but died before presenting the adoption to the Crown as a transfer of the banner. No controlling judgment decides whether adoption alone carries that public office.

## Six banners, five banners, or none

A final succession judgment requires six of the nine sitting banners, including two seasons. A temporary emergency regency requires five and may be limited to the Sunseed undertaking. The court may instead divide household duties without a vote or leave the seat vacant. Any bearer or regent may cast only the authority the judgment actually grants; a changed undertaking, unauthorized covenant, or term beyond that authority may require renewed judgment.

## What judgment may and may not settle

Mirath's claim concerns public office, blood continuity, and proven capacity. Aven's concerns the obligations created by chosen kinship and valid adoption. Neither claim is fraudulent merely because it leaves the other legal noun unresolved. The current holder, regency, doctrine, seal, support, and later succession outcome remain products of play, and both claimants remain political actors after judgment.

references.title: The Pall
references.summary: A self-sustaining Shadowfell siege-work is replacing Orison's daylight, memory, and seasons and will close the last usable road after Court Day Seven.
references.content:
## Dusk after the host has gone

The Pall is the Shadowfell siege-work raised over Orison. The host that kindled it was driven away, but the work continued without its makers, replacing daylight, remembered weather, and seasonal change with permanent dusk. Ordinary forces can hold parts of the perimeter and evacuate some people; they cannot preserve the city intact.

## The ring closes at moonrise

The Pall completed its outer ring on the night before Aurelune's opening audience. At moonrise after Court Day Seven it closes the Lantern Road, erases the remaining planar approaches, and begins sustaining itself. The Crown Passage can still place the Sunseed's root-casket at Orison's western gate before that closure, and one road from the gate still reaches the Pall's center. This passage deadline is distinct from the custody term, which begins when the Sunseed is uprooted.

## Which rescue the Sunseed performs

A stone from Orison's noon market remembers warmth and shadow beneath the Sunseed, demonstrating the remedy. Properly borne and planted at the Pall's center, the relic can force the blighted region to remember its rightful sky. Breaking the siege-work, restoring natural day, preserving Orison, and evacuating its people remain legally and operationally different possible undertakings.

references.title: The Concord of Open Hands
references.summary: Aurelune's constitutional path lets seven seasonally balanced Great Banners compel joint custody of a royal relic through one certified, governable undertaking.
references.content:
## Seven seals and every season

The Concord of Open Hands permits seven of Aurelune's ten Great Banners to compel the Crown to place a royal relic in joint custody for one named undertaking. Spring, Summer, Autumn, and Winter must all be represented. The exact petition must name a maximum term, preserve a royal interest, and state custody, command, liability, recall, return, and the undertaking it serves.

## Seal, certification, acceptance, joinder

Banner seals supply the lawful majority. The Lord Chamberlain certifies that one internally consistent instrument was lawfully adopted; Theron's certification and House Eiral's political seal are separate acts. Orison's acceptance does not replace banner seals. The king cannot veto a valid Concord and may join only after certification; royal joinder improves cooperation without creating validity.

## What a changed word releases

A material amendment releases every seal whose stated ground depends on the changed text. Corrected exact language may be reaffirmed in the same sitting. Associated covenants may carry recognition, finance, surety, deployment, or credit when they remain public, enforceable, and compatible with the central petition. The Concord creates no general right to every royal relic unless the enacted text actually does so.

references.title: The Oath of the Unbroken Word
references.summary: Aurelune's court oath forbids knowing falsehood and bad-faith sealing while leaving omission, narrow scope, and selective context as political weapons.
references.content:
## The leaves turn toward the speaker

Every sovereign, peer, officer, advocate, and recognized petitioner speaking beneath the Argent Canopy swears not to assert what they believe false, deny what they believe true, or seal words they do not intend to bind them. A knowing violation takes the speaker's court voice for a year and causes the court's mirrors to repeat the broken sentence. The sanction is real; the court does not secretly lie around it.

## Truth without completeness

The Oath of the Unbroken Word does not require relevance, completeness, cooperation, ordinary-language scope where precedent supplies a narrower one, or a stable future intention that has not been promised. Omission, selected categories, convenient ignorance, accurate but incomplete precedent, and answers to narrower questions remain lawful techniques.

## What mirrors and seals preserve

Oath-mirrors can preserve an exact public declaration and the question left unanswered. A declaration binds reputation and witnesses, not the final vote. The oath forbids a speaker from sealing words they do not intend to obey; it does not keep a material amendment from releasing a prior seal or make several incompatible private meanings into one governable instrument.

references.title: The Lantern Road Compact
references.summary: Orison's compact guarantees an emergency audience and access to a Crown Passage, but not treaty equality, custody, or command of the rescue.
references.content:
## An audience and one Crown Passage

The Lantern Road Compact between Orison and Aurelune guarantees Orison an emergency audience and access to a Crown Passage. Together with the surviving council's sealed commission, it gives Orison recognized standing to petition during the Pall emergency. It does not itself decide whether the city enters as an independent polity, royal guest, or jointly sponsored petitioner.

## Standing is not sovereignty

The compact does not recognize Orison as Aurelune's treaty equal, transfer custody of the Sunseed, appoint an expedition commander, or authorize the Crown to govern Orison. Those questions require the Concord petition, Orison's acceptance, or separate instruments. Passage access and political status remain distinct authorities.

## The road closes before the loan begins

The Crown Passage can carry the root-casket to Orison's western gate before moonrise after Court Day Seven. One road from that gate still remembers the way to the Pall's center. Once the Pall closes the Lantern Road and begins sustaining itself, the passage cannot cross the ring. This travel deadline does not start or shorten the custody term, which begins only when the Sunseed is uprooted.

encounters.title: The Argent Canopy
encounters.summary: Caelir's refusal leaves lawful nouns open; beneath the listening Canopy, Orison must name the standing, purpose, and calendar around which banners can gather.
encounters.opening_view: Mara lays Orison's black-frosted stone beneath the throne. The Sunseed warms it; a market-stall shadow opens across the marble, sharp as noon. Ten banners watch. Four seasonal aisles stand empty. Theron has left seven seal lines beside a calendar ending at moonrise. Caelir waits until the frost is water. "I refuse this undertaking," he says. He does not refuse the rescue.
encounters.content:
## Situation

The Argent Canopy hangs above the throne hall: a living crown of silver leaves, each turned toward whoever presently holds the right to speak. Beneath King Caelir III's throne, the Sunseed burns inside a root of clear glass. Its light climbs through the floor and lays the same mild dawn across every face, kind and cruel alike.

Orison's emergency delegation is received on the first morning after the Pall completes its outer ring around the city. The Shadowfell host that kindled it has been driven away; the siege-work has continued without its makers. Mara Venn has brought a paving stone from Orison's noon market. Beneath the Sunseed it warms, sheds black frost, and casts the sharp shadow it cast before the sky failed. Aurelune's Dawnward keepers have repeated the test. Caelir accepts that the relic can restore Orison's day.

Seven court days remain before the Pall closes the Lantern Road and begins feeding itself. The Crown Passage can still carry the Sunseed to Orison's western gate before the last open road to the Pall's center closes at moonrise. The loan term begins when the relic is uprooted; the road deadline determines whether the undertaking can begin at all.

Caelir also knows that uprooting the Sunseed will thin the Dawnward, disturb the seasonal roads, and teach every neighboring realm that sufficient need may put a royal trust to a vote. He refuses with a sentence polished for the record:

> I will not place the Sunseed beyond the custody of my Crown for the undertaking you have proposed.

The sentence leaves travel, joint custody, and a different undertaking open. Half the court hears the doors.

Lord Chamberlain Theron Eiral reads the Concord of Open Hands. Seven Great Banners may compel joint custody of a royal relic for one named undertaking. Spring, Summer, Autumn, and Winter must all stand among them. The petition must preserve a royal interest and state custody, command, term, liability, recall, and return. Theron must certify a valid instrument and must refuse an inconsistent one.

No one lowers their voice. As each recognized speaker answers, a band of leaves turns toward that voice and remains there until the court accepts a different relation among Crown, banner, relic, and city. The hall begins the week already shaped by incompatible truths.

## The voices beneath the Canopy

The first positions arrive like blades laid on the table.

- **Caelir:** “I can save those whom my roads can carry. I will not promise a city where I can promise lives.”
- **Theron Eiral, in office:** “Seven, with every season. The number and the balance are separate questions.”
- **Saelira Ilyrion:** “Do not rescue a people into ownership.”
- **Othalan Maelith:** “Name the person who will answer when the city cannot.”
- **Ysandre Serathiel:** “Compassion has given us a destination. It has not given us command.”
- **Avar Vaudren:** “Before we save Orison, perhaps someone will decide who is permitted to be seen saving it.”
- **Mirelle Orelle:** “Whose village is paying for the generosity presently admired in this hall?”
- **Pelion Namaris:** “Which sentence should a hostile court quote from us in a hundred years?”
- **Eirath Thalan:** “Need may be urgent without being constitutional.”
- **Caldus Serevin:** “What stands east when the Sunseed does not?”
- **Mirath Avarre:** “A banner cannot be inherited by wishing blood irrelevant.”
- **Aven Tal:** “Nor by pretending an adoption was a household decoration.”

Every sentence is defensible. None gives away the bargain.

## What the first audience establishes

The campaign's machinery is public. Before the audience ends, plain questions establish:

- seven seals are required, and the four-season requirement is independent of the count;
- Theron's duty to certify is not House Eiral's decision to seal;
- the Lantern Road compact guarantees Orison an emergency audience and a usable Crown Passage, not treaty equality;
- the Sunseed must enter the passage before moonrise after Court Day Seven, while the custody term begins only when the relic is uprooted;
- declarations bind reputation and witnesses, not the final vote;
- the Ashen Bough can be seated only if its hearing enters the calendar now;
- Caelir may file a narrower royal instrument or join a certified Concord later;
- Crown title can survive joint possession and use; and
- house bargains may sit in indexed side covenants, provided they do not contradict the central petition.

The doors are public; preference hides in the nouns.

## Choices made before leaving the hall

### Standing

Orison's sealed emergency mandate and Lantern Road compact secure recognized-petitioner status, not treaty equality. Choose the entry: agents of an independent polity, royal guests seeking relief, or joint petitioners with an Eladrin sponsor.

- **Sovereign-petitioner standing** strengthens Ilyrion and Aven Tal, but makes Maelith's preferred wardship settlement harder to present as benign. It gives Orison a voice in this proceeding without deciding the broader status Ilyrion wants.
- **Royal-guest standing** gives the petitioners protection and access, but allows Caelir to frame every concession as generosity to dependents.
- **Joint sponsorship** accelerates access to one house and lets that house claim early authorship.

Theron permits all three. He dips the pen after the petitioners choose the noun.

### Public purpose

Give the court one sentence describing the work. Saving Orison, restoring natural day, preserving the seasonal cycle, resisting Shadowfell expansion, and honoring an alliance lead to different bargains. Every house will quote this sentence when the draft asks it to accept an inconvenient term.

### The royal offer

Caelir opens evacuation gates immediately and orders his officers to prepare a six-day Crown expedition as a fallback. That expedition cannot become executable until the court has costed a substitute Dawnward, opened the passages, and settled command; the same public work that strengthens the petition may also strengthen the king's rival instrument. Accepting the gates does not waive the Sunseed petition unless Orison's petitioners say it does. Refusing them preserves bargaining clarity but costs mortal lives if the court fails. Accepting while continuing the petition is possible, though the king will truthfully describe Orison's petitioners as having accepted his plan.

### Calendar

Request an accelerated hearing calendar, public appointments, private consultations, or an early drafting session. The Chamberlain grants time according to constitutional priority rather than courtesy. A formal Ashen Bough hearing must be requested now or it cannot be concluded before the Conclave without displacing another public proceeding.

## Opening strategies

### Announce a broad concord

Seek eight or more seals, preserve a royal role, and frame the rescue as a shared defense of natural order. This attracts Eiral and Thalan, but gives reformers and martial houses less partisan credit.

### Build a minimum coalition quickly

Approach the easiest seven banners and plan to settle inconsistencies in drafting. This conserves time and invites the king to attack the coalition at its weakest seams.

### Lead with Orison's equality

Make political recognition part of the rescue from the beginning. Ilyrion and Aven become natural allies. Maelith, Orelle, and Thalan require careful separation between sovereign status and enforceable security.

### Lead with Aurelune's security

Begin by funding wards, reserves, and return guarantees. Serathiel, Serevin, Orelle, and Thalan become more accessible. Orison may be rescued under terms that turn it into the object of an Eladrin military undertaking.

### Accept the king's frame, then narrow it

Treat exclusive royal command as a starting point and bargain for joint custody, purpose-limited vetoes, or a mortal co-custodian. This can produce a voluntary royal joinder, but it makes a cleanly independent petition harder.

## Where the first audience can end

### The court opens cleanly

The petitioners gain recognized standing, a usable calendar, an unambiguous statement of the Concord, and at least three houses willing to receive immediate proposals. The royal evacuation offer remains available without being treated as settlement.

### Access purchased with position

- The petitioners gain access by accepting one house as sponsor; that house claims precedence over the coalition.
- The petitioners secure an accelerated calendar by making all appointments public; later compromises become harder to describe differently to different houses.
- The petitioners accept evacuation gates; lives are saved, but Caelir gains a truthful public claim that his plan is already in operation.

### The king leaves with the only public plan

Refuse to state standing or purpose and spend the audience contesting the king's motives. The court still opens. The petitioners leave with fewer appointments, while Caelir's evacuation instrument becomes the only plan in the hall that already has roads, officers, and a timetable.

## Enter in the public record

- the noun used for Orison's standing;
- the public purpose announced beneath the Canopy;
- whether evacuation gates were accepted;
- whether the Ashen Bough hearing was calendared;
- which house, if any, became the first sponsor; and
- whether the petitioners publicly committed to a broad concord or a seven-seal victory.

## Returning beneath the Canopy

The Canopy remains available for formal declarations, royal counteroffers, and changes to the public calendar. Returning here is never neutral. A statement made beneath the silver leaves is heard as a bid to define the whole court's business.

encounters.title: The Unfurling Branch
encounters.summary: Ilyrion offers Spring only if Orison enters the rescue as a polity with an operative hand in its own preservation.
encounters.opening_view: Silver shears close, but not on the pear branch. Saelira lifts the boundary marker it crossed and plants it farther out. Behind her, mortal trees bear plaques reading treaty, gift, theft, rescue, defiance. Rethan Sol sets two blank instruments on the soil: one preserves Crown title; the other leaves room for Orison's own hand. Saelira plants the shears between them. No one has decided which document must come first.
encounters.content:
## Situation

House Ilyrion receives petitioners in a terraced conservatory where mortal trees grow among flowers that bloom only in the first hour of Spring. Each tree bears a plaque naming the treaty, gift, theft, rescue, or act of defiance by which it came to Aurelune. Lady Saelira Ilyrion conducts the audience with silver shears in hand. Whenever a branch crosses its allotted border, she decides whether to prune it or move the marker.

Saelira wants the Sunseed used. She also wants the rescue to prove that mortal polities may enter Aurelune's highest acts as parties rather than dependents. She will not spend her banner on a petition that calls Orison a ward, places every mortal beneath Eladrin command, or treats consent as a door that can be closed only once.

Her offer is plain enough to quote and broad enough to fight over:

> House Ilyrion will seal an undertaking in which Orison stands as a party to its own preservation.

She leaves the binding surface open and gives the court a sentence by which to measure any retreat.

## House Ilyrion

- **Lady Saelira Ilyrion** is generous, ambitious, and pleased when the generous act also wins the argument she has wanted for a century.
- **Rethan Sol**, her jurist, knows how to make reciprocal obligations remain reciprocal after the stronger party begins “protecting” the weaker.
- **Envoy Mara Venn** wants recognition and mistrusts language Orison cannot honor while half its government is underground.
- **Aven Tal** appears often enough that every Ilyrion concession is also read as a vote in the Ashen succession.

Saelira practices moral compression. Every personal surety becomes wardship; every reservation about recognition becomes a taste for domination. Her examples are genuine, and her categories leave compromise looking shameful.

Ask her what authority she will allow an expedition commander inside the named undertaking. Ask whether sovereign partners may owe indemnity. Ask which recognition term must be operative now and which may live in a witnessed compact. She answers each narrower question cleanly.

## What Spring must recognize

Ilyrion needs three things, though they need not all occupy the same document:

1. Orison is named a treaty partner, co-principal, or sovereign participant rather than a ward.
2. A mortal representative holds real custody, oversight, or authority over the undertaking.
3. Orison may refuse a redirection of the undertaking or a use against its civil government.

A side compact, declaration, or reciprocal custody protocol can carry part of the bargain if another credible banner guarantees it. Saelira cares less about the binding surface than about whether the power survives translation into that surface.

## Forms Saelira will accept

### Full recognition in the petition

The petition names Orison as a treaty partner and co-custodian. This is the clearest route to Ilyrion's seal and the hardest route through Maelith and Thalan.

### Recognition by side compact

The central petition remains narrow. A parallel compact, witnessed by Eiral or Namaris, recognizes Orison's standing and limits later Eladrin direction. Ilyrion accepts this if the side instrument is adopted before its seal is fixed.

### Reciprocal personal surety

A named Orison envoy and a named Eladrin noble each enter the other's protection for the duration. Ilyrion can treat this as equality rather than wardship. Maelith can treat the same arrangement as personal security.

### Public guarantee by a third banner

Another house promises to oppose any use of the expedition to subordinate Orison. Eiral, Namaris, or even Vaudren can make the promise meaningful. A private assurance is not enough.

### Aven Tal's accession

If Aven is seated and seals on recognition grounds, Ilyrion can accept a narrower central clause because the coalition itself now embodies the principle. This route ties Orison's rescue to a disputed inheritance rule.

## The draft waiting on the table

Saelira asks Orison's petitioners to approve a declaration titled **The Equal Dawn**. Its strongest clause states that no Eladrin commander may alter the expedition's purpose without the consent of Orison's co-custodian. Serathiel reads this as an operational veto. Maelith reads the title as an accusation. Thalan reads the declaration as a general constitutional proposition hidden inside emergency relief.

Sign, revise, defer, or replace the text. Saelira will state exactly what was accepted. A tolerable revision has no public life until she writes it.

## Ways to turn the Spring banner

### Adopt the Equal Dawn

Ilyrion becomes declared immediately. The coalition gains a clear reformist center and makes military and dynastic compromises more expensive.

### Separate status from command

Recognize Orison as sovereign while defining a narrow military chain of command. This can satisfy Ilyrion and Serathiel if command cannot change the undertaking itself.

### Build reciprocal guarantees

Bring Maelith, Namaris, or Eiral into the conservatory and trades personal surety for political equality. The resulting settlement is more durable and gives every participant less than its preferred language.

### Promise a later constitutional compact

Ilyrion may declare support for a narrow rescue petition if a second instrument is calendared before the Conclave. Saelira demands a sponsor and a date, not an aspiration.

### Refuse to constitutionalize the rescue

Ilyrion does not become an enemy. Saelira may still seal a text that prevents wardship in practice. What the petitioners lose is the first Spring banner willing to say, before witnesses, that Orison enters as an equal.

## How Spring may leave the branch

### A usable Spring declaration

Ilyrion declares support on terms compatible with at least one plausible Maelith or Serathiel settlement. The petitioners obtain a drafted recognition clause or side compact rather than a verbal understanding.

### Recognition with a bearer

- Ilyrion declares for full recognition, and Maelith announces that no personal surety can coexist with the adopted language.
- Ilyrion accepts reciprocal surety, but Mara Venn or another mortal representative must personally bear the risk.
- A later compact wins Ilyrion, but the court calendar becomes tighter and Eiral demands a credible sponsor.

### Principle without a seal

Accept Ilyrion's rhetoric without fixing any operative language. Saelira praises the coalition publicly but does not declare. Other houses react to the broad principle while the coalition has gained no seal.

## Record before leaving

- Orison's named political status;
- the identity and powers of any mortal co-custodian;
- whether the Equal Dawn or a replacement declaration is public;
- whether recognition sits in the petition or a side compact;
- whether Aven Tal's claim has become part of the coalition; and
- what right Orison retains if Eladrin command changes the undertaking.

## On a return

Ilyrion is easiest to revisit after another house proposes language that appears protective but changes Orison's status. Saelira will trade breadth of recognition for stronger enforcement, or stronger symbolism for a narrower operative clause. She will not pretend those are the same victory.

reference_links.context: States Orison's recognition aim and limits promises the besieged government cannot honor.
Tests whether rescue recognizes a mortal polity as a partner or merely protects a dependent.
Its limited recognition can support petitioner standing while leaving Orison's broader political status unsettled.

encounters.title: The Gallery of Silver Kin
encounters.summary: Maelith demands a living guarantor whose obligations survive command changes without quietly making Orison a ward.
encounters.opening_view: The empty family chair has already been moved beside Mara Venn. Across from it, Lady Senra rests one hand on an unsigned reciprocal bond. Master Halven turns a plaque between protected guest and fosterling while Othalan recites the offered comforts: rank, household, residence, protection. None is false. Then he asks who will answer, in a living name, if the Sunseed does not return.
encounters.content:
## Situation

The Gallery of Silver Kin contains no antlers. Its walls are crowded with the people House Maelith acquired by birth, marriage, adoption, fosterage, hostage exchange, sworn friendship, and negotiated protection. Each portrait bears a silver plaque naming the relation. The plaques are exact. The painted faces are serene.

Prince-Regent Othalan Maelith does not object to saving Orison. He objects to trusting a city, an army, or a temporary coalition with the return of the Sunseed. A city cannot be shamed, married, disinherited, confined, or made to answer before a household court. A named person can.

> House Maelith will not demand that Orison become our ward. We require a person whom the law can hold.

His first proposed person is Envoy Mara Venn. The instrument calls her a fostered guest, preserves her rank and household, guarantees her comfort, and gives Maelith authority over her movement and future succession claims. Othalan has not lied about a single protection. He has merely begun with the warmest column of the ledger.

## House Maelith

- **Prince-Regent Othalan Maelith** trusts obligations that can sit at a table, inherit an estate, and be shamed by name.
- **Lady Senra Maelith**, his eldest daughter, offers herself as reciprocal surety without pretending the gesture is symbolic.
- **Master Halven Roe**, Keeper of Relations, can recite the powers of fosterling, hostage, ward, adopted child, and protected guest without consulting a book.
- **Lord Avar Vaudren** is present even when absent; one place in the last equinox procession still governs who may stand beside whom.

Othalan governs through kinship nouns. He begins with education, safety, dignity, and affection; residence, marriage, departure, and succession wait for a narrower question. He never misstates the bond. He begins where it sounds most like love.

## What the White Hart must recognize

Maelith will seal when a named person, office, or estate can be made to answer for custody and return. The guarantee must survive a change in command and cannot rest on Orison's ruined treasury or the petitioners' good intentions.

Othalan will accept:

1. narrow temporary fosterage stripped of unwanted family powers;
2. reciprocal hostages or protected guests;
3. personal guarantees by Great Banners;
4. a Namaris bond enforceable against named estates; or
5. a royal co-custodian whose office answers for return.

He will trade control for answerability. He will not accept sincerity as a legal person.

## Relations Othalan will recognize

### Narrow fosterage

Mara Venn or another senior representative becomes Maelith's fosterling for thirteen days. Strip succession, marriage, residence, and command from the instrument while preserving protection and answerability. Othalan asks what remains of the guarantee.

### Reciprocal hostages

Lady Senra travels under Orison's protection while a mortal representative resides with Maelith. This satisfies Ilyrion more readily and creates a severe personal cost if the undertaking fails.

### Banner surety

Two or more houses pledge their estates or offices to answer for return. Orelle can value the risk; Namaris can define default; Thalan approves the constitutional restraint. The coalition must decide which houses will expose themselves.

### Royal co-custody

A named Crown representative remains physically with the Sunseed. This is Maelith's easiest non-familial settlement and makes independent mortal command harder.

### Marriage or adoption compact

A marriage promise or sealed adoption can satisfy Maelith and transform succession politics. No one at court calls marriage or adoption symbolic. Use either only when the adventurers are willing to inherit the relation along with the seal.

## The Vaudren grievance

Maelith's seal cannot be discussed in isolation from the Red Rose. Othalan claims that the previous procession followed the genealogical order recorded in the Gallery. Vaudren claims the procession was a political act that publicly diminished his house.

Othalan first offers sorrow for whatever pain accompanied the correct order. The apology concedes feeling, preserves the act, and satisfies no one who came to change the record. He can be pushed toward one of three meaningful concessions:

- acknowledge that he chose the order rather than merely followed it;
- state that Vaudren's precedence is equal in the present undertaking; or
- accept neutral authorship under Eiral rather than Maelith leadership.

A private apology protects his dignity. A public one can win Vaudren.

## Ways to bring the Hart beside Orison

### Draft narrow fosterage

Turn Maelith's preferred form into a limited security instrument. This is exacting work, but it can coexist with Orison's sovereignty.

### Offer reciprocal surety

Lady Senra's willingness makes this real. The arrangement may satisfy Ilyrion and Maelith together, while drawing the rescue into personal succession politics.

### Assemble banner guarantors

Shift risk from a mortal person to allied houses. Orelle and Namaris become important; the coalition gains durability and more veto points.

### Preserve royal co-custody

Maelith declares readily if a named royal custodian remains. Serathiel and Thalan approve. Ilyrion requires a mortal co-custodian with actual authority.

### Settle Vaudren first

Ask Othalan to make a public concession before discussing his seal. This can unlock two Summer and Spring relationships at once, or make Maelith feel it has paid before receiving anything.

## How the Hart may leave the Gallery

### Answerability without subordination

Maelith declares on a precise form of personal surety that does not silently subordinate Orison and does not foreclose Vaudren's support.

### Bonds that bite

- A mortal envoy accepts fosterage and loses meaningful freedom for the duration.
- Lady Senra becomes reciprocal surety, binding Maelith strongly and exposing her to the expedition's dangers.
- Royal co-custody wins Maelith but gives the Crown a practical means to slow or redirect the undertaking.
- Maelith apologizes publicly and joins, while its followers demand senior credit elsewhere.

### The warm noun remains undefined

Accept the phrase protected guest without defining Maelith's powers. Ilyrion reacts as though wardship has been conceded, while Othalan still refuses to declare until the legal instrument is complete.

## Record before leaving

- the named person or office answering for the Sunseed;
- the powers attached to fosterage, protection, or hostage status;
- whether surety is reciprocal;
- which estates or banners guarantee return;
- the status of the Vaudren grievance; and
- whether Maelith expects senior authorship or accepts neutral credit.

## On a return

Every custody change reopens Maelith's bargain. Othalan is willing to exchange stronger personal security for less command, or weaker personal control for broader banner guarantees. He does not accept that a coalition's sincerity is itself an enforceable relation.

reference_links.context: Becomes Maelith's proposed personal surety, exposing the line between protection, fosterage, and confinement.
Personal surety must protect answerable people without converting Orison's civil authority into wardship.

encounters.title: The Noon Spear Court
encounters.summary: Serathiel puts command, eastern defense, and the loan term on one war table and asks which orders remain executable.
encounters.opening_view: A brass company slides one valley east. Three hands reach for it; Ysandre's spear-butt strikes the glass before any can claim command. One baton points toward Orison, one to the eastern marches, one across the Crown Passage. Beyond them, wardstones remain unbought and reserves unordered. "The Sunseed can save Orison," Ysandre says. "Now tell me which realm goes undefended while it does."
encounters.content:
## Situation

The Noon Spear Court is a parade ground beneath a sky fixed at high summer. Maps lie under glass in the paving stones. Brass companies move across the eastern marches, the roads to Orison, and the dark ring of the Pall as messengers alter the estimates. No one contests the distances. The dispute is over whose hand may move the pieces.

Marshal Ysandre Serathiel grants Orison's premise before anyone can accuse her of hiding behind doubt:

> The Sunseed can save Orison. An uncommanded Sunseed can lose two kingdoms.

Ysandre wants one expedition commander with authority over route, protection, tempo, and return. She prefers herself or a royal officer. She also wants soldiers, wards, or allies placed on the eastern border before the Sunseed leaves.

The danger is real. The Dawnward will thin. The Gloam Host will see it. A thirteen-day expedition needs guards, engineers, transport, reserve plans, and an answer for the hour when the road and the border both fail. Serathiel's deception lies elsewhere: she presents the assumptions favorable to her command as though they arrived with the terrain.

## House Serathiel

- **Marshal Ysandre Serathiel** hears every promise as an order missing authority, supply, or contingency.
- **Captain Naevra Sol** commands the Sunlance Guard and can guard the Crown's interest without commanding the entire expedition.
- **Strategist Corven Ashe** has prepared several workable divisions of authority. He begins with the one Ysandre prefers.
- **Envoy Mara Venn** can say what Orison will accept from an allied commander and what it will treat as foreign rule.

Ysandre deceives by choosing the conditions under which only her solution works. No new allied troops. No substitute ward. No divided command. No shorter term. Under those assumptions, her conclusion is often impeccable. Ask for the assumptions and the other war plans appear.

## What the Noon Spear must recognize

Serathiel needs three functions filled:

1. one coherent expedition command;
2. a reserve, substitute ward, or allied force protecting Aurelune; and
3. an answer to delay, route change, and a genuine border emergency.

House Serathiel requires simultaneous dangers to produce orders, not a committee in which every member discovers a veto.

## Command structures on the table

### Eladrin expedition command

Serathiel or a royal officer commands the whole undertaking. This is militarily simple, wins several conservative houses, and risks turning Orison's rescue into an intervention governed from Aurelune.

### Divided command by purpose

Command movement and use of the Sunseed. Captain Naevra commands its guard. Orison's envoy controls consent to any change in the named undertaking. The arrangement can work if disputes have a defined arbiter and no role can veto ordinary action by silence.

### Purpose-limited royal veto

A royal co-custodian may stop actions that would damage the Sunseed, exceed the undertaking, or violate an objective recall trigger. This preserves a royal interest without giving the Crown general command.

### Replacement reserve

Mortal allies, another Eladrin house, or hired fey troops reinforce the eastern marches. Serathiel accepts troops under Serevin's border command even if she does not command the expedition.

### Substitute Dawnward

Orelle finances temporary wards, Namaris defines performance, and Serevin identifies the vulnerable crossings. This is expensive and can satisfy Serathiel without moving large formations.

### Shorter term

A six-day loan sharply reduces risk to Aurelune. It may be operationally insufficient for Orison. Serathiel will not describe the shorter term as sufficient unless asked the exact probability of success.

## The war-table test

Serathiel invites the adventurers to issue orders for three simultaneous events:

- the expedition road divides around a Shadowfell incursion;
- the Dawnward reports a confirmed breach; and
- Orison's co-custodian refuses a route that places the Sunseed under exclusive royal control.

The exercise records whose authority the adventurers expect to prevail. Each answer becomes a draft command principle that other houses may quote.

Refuse the staged crisis and demand every written alternative. Corven produces five command schemes, including two withheld from the opening exercise. Ysandre respects an answer that survives the table.

## Ways to turn the Summer spear

### Give Serathiel command

The house declares immediately and provides a complete escort. Ilyrion and Orison demand purpose limits; Vaudren may resent military authorship.

### Build divided command

Distinguish custody, protection, operational command, and political consent. This can support a broad coalition and creates more points at which a crisis can deadlock.

### Secure the border first

Bring Serevin, Orelle, or allied commanders into the Court and close the military objection materially. Serathiel then bargains over expedition command rather than existential risk.

### Accept a short term with extension machinery

The petition begins with six days and permits extension by several custodians if objective milestones are met. Thalan approves the restraint. Orison bears the danger of delay.

### Reject command as a price of compassion

Serathiel remains opposed but may provide technical assistance. A coalition can win without this Summer banner; the king's charge of military irresponsibility becomes stronger.

## How the Spear may leave the table

### Orders everyone can obey

Serathiel declares on a command scheme that protects Aurelune without giving any one actor the practical power to defeat the undertaking for unrelated reasons.

### Command with a price

- Exclusive command wins the seal and narrows Orison's independence.
- Divided command preserves politics but requires an arbiter, delay rule, and deadlock procedure.
- Substitute wards protect Aurelune but create debt, audit, and maintenance obligations.
- A shorter term wins conservative support and makes the expedition's margin thin.

### Everyone can stop the expedition

Promise everyone a veto over the dangers they fear. Serathiel demonstrates that the Sunseed could remain motionless while every actor truthfully waits for another's consent. No seal is declared until the command text is repaired.

## Write into the campaign order

- the named expedition commander;
- the distinction between custody, guard command, political consent, and operational authority;
- the eastern reserve or substitute ward package;
- the response to an objective border breach;
- the initial term and any extension rule; and
- whether the war-table principles became public.

## On a return

Serathiel is easiest to revisit after Serevin or Orelle has put troops, wards, and payment on the table. She may surrender the baton itself; she will not accept a plan whose orders disappear when two dangers arrive at once.

reference_links.context: Defines what Orison can accept from allied command without yielding its civil government.
Defines the expedition-command problem and exposes assumptions that make one military structure appear inevitable.
Distinguishes expedition command from authority over the eastern marches and requires a real substitute defense.
Expedition command may govern operations without governing Orison or redirecting the undertaking against its consent.
Its route and operational requirements make command, transport, and contingency concrete rather than ceremonial.
Its movement, protection, and permitted uses define the command bargain and eastern-defense risk.

encounters.title: The Red Rose Pavilion
encounters.summary: Vaudren makes an old precedence wound public and demands satisfaction that carries responsibility rather than costume.
encounters.opening_view: The musicians begin three different entrances and stop at the same sour chord. Six servants still hold the pavilion open: white carpet, twilight runner, bare red cloth. Avar Vaudren waits beneath a thornwood crown trained around one deliberate gap; Senra's place card stands a handspan before his heir's. He does not ask which entrance is fair. He asks which one the court is meant to remember.
encounters.content:
## Situation

The Red Rose Pavilion is built anew for every audience. Silk walls, thornwood poles, carpets, flowers, musicians, and even the direction of entry are selected to state the host's judgment before the host speaks. Three arrangements await Orison's petitioners. The servants need only learn whether Maelith, Eiral, or no sponsor will cross the threshold first.

Lord Avar Vaudren does not ask whether Orison deserves rescue. He asks what the rescue will make true at court and whose name will be attached to it.

At the previous equinox procession, Maelith placed Lady Senra before Vaudren's heir. Maelith calls the order genealogically correct. Vaudren calls it a deliberate public diminution. The oath permits both statements.

Avar receives the petitioners beneath a trellis trained into the shape of a crown with one missing thorn.

> House Vaudren will not place its rose beneath a hart that has not acknowledged where it stepped.

He will join after public satisfaction, equal precedence for this undertaking, or a settlement in which neither house leads. Private peace is welcome. It is not the same thing as a repaired public order.

## House Vaudren

- **Lord Avar Vaudren** knows that precedence controls invitations, sponsorship, command, and whose account becomes the court's memory.
- **Lord Cael Vaudren**, his heir, would accept a restrained settlement and will not purchase it by contradicting his father before witnesses.
- **Mistress Ivara Quill**, herald of the house, records entrances, titles, silences, and acknowledgments with equal care.
- **Othalan Maelith** can end the quarrel by owning a chosen act, deepen it with an apology for pain, or step aside for neutral authorship.

Avar deceives through the measuring stick. No house has sacrificed more—if one begins the count with Vaudren's greatest campaign. No apology is more unprecedented—if adequacy is never mentioned. He presents rank as a fact while selecting the interval, witness, and ceremony by which rank is measured.

## What the Red Rose must recognize

Vaudren will seal through any one of four doors:

1. Othalan publicly acknowledges the chosen act that diminished Vaudren;
2. the court fixes equal or alternating precedence for this undertaking;
3. neither Maelith nor Vaudren receives authorship of the coalition; or
4. Vaudren bears a visible office or risk that creates independent honor in the rescue.

A private apology may reconcile two people. It repairs nothing at court unless Avar chooses to put the reconciliation where the injury occurred: before witnesses.

## Satisfactions Avar will own

### Exact apology

The meaningful formula is not apology for pain. Maelith must acknowledge choice and consequence:

> I chose an order that diminished House Vaudren before the court. I did not intend every consequence, and the choice was mine.

Othalan may alter the last clause, offer equal precedence now, or accept neutral authorship instead. The exact words determine whether Avar calls the matter satisfied.

### Adjudicated precedence

Namaris can identify the legal difference between genealogical precedence and ceremonial precedence. Eiral can chair a determination limited to the Sunseed undertaking. This resolves the present coalition without deciding every future procession.

### Neutral authorship

The petition is presented as an act of the whole court under Eiral or under no house name. Vaudren accepts if Maelith also renounces senior credit. Several other houses dislike losing public ownership of their concessions.

### The Rose bears the visible risk

Vaudren can provide the public champion, co-custodian, escort, or guarantor. The house gains honor through service rather than precedence. Serathiel contests military roles; Maelith may offer Lady Senra for the same purpose.

### Formal challenge

Vaudren may demand a ceremonial contest of advocacy, endurance, or arms. It assigns satisfaction under court custom, not truth. Serve as advocate, judge, second, or refuse the spectacle.

## Public and private settlement

Avar offers an easy private bargain: Maelith sends a personal apology, Vaudren privately promises not to obstruct, and neither house changes its public account. This may calm the feud. It does not produce a declared seal and remains vulnerable to later claims about leadership.

A public bargain is harder because every noun creates precedent. It is also more stable. The Masque of Plain Faces provides the strongest venue, but the Pavilion can host witnesses immediately if the petitioners want speed.

## Ways to bring the Rose into the same procession

### Demand the apology now

Bring Maelith into the Pavilion and resolves the grievance before either house seals. This can win both houses and lets the argument consume the coalition's first public day.

### Move to neutral authorship

Deny both houses senior credit. Eiral becomes more important. Vaudren can declare without forgiveness, and Maelith must decide whether security matters more than precedence.

### Give Vaudren an independent office

A Vaudren co-custodian, guarantor, or public advocate creates honor without rewriting procession law. The office must have real responsibility, not merely costume.

### Accept private reconciliation

The personal feud cools. Vaudren remains open rather than declared until the public record changes elsewhere.

### Exclude the grievance from the rescue

Tell both houses their quarrel is irrelevant. This may impress Ilyrion and Serathiel. Vaudren will not seal a coalition that allows Maelith to lead under cover of urgency.

## How the Rose may leave the pavilion

### Satisfaction before witnesses

Vaudren declares through public satisfaction or a durable neutral-credit arrangement that does not require humiliating Maelith.

### Honor purchased elsewhere

- Maelith apologizes publicly and demands greater control over custody or surety in return.
- Vaudren receives a real expedition office, adding another authority to the command structure.
- Neutral authorship wins Vaudren and Eiral while disappointing houses that need visible credit.
- A formal challenge settles custom and makes the court remember the rescue as Vaudren's arena.

### Courtesy without repair

Accept a graceful private apology and announce that the grievance is resolved. Avar truthfully states that no public satisfaction occurred. Maelith truthfully states that it apologized. Both accounts weaken the petitioners' credibility.

## What the heralds will repeat

- whether Maelith acknowledged choice and consequence;
- the public or private status of any reconciliation;
- the coalition's authorship and credit formula;
- any Vaudren office in custody, escort, or advocacy;
- the current rule of precedence for the undertaking; and
- whether the Masque must ratify the settlement.

## On a return

Vaudren becomes relevant whenever the coalition changes who speaks first, signs first, commands publicly, or receives credit. Avar can yield the old grievance for a visible present office. He will not accept that visible order is merely symbolic when every other house is using it to measure power.

encounters.title: The Golden Sheaf Exchange
encounters.summary: Orelle prices the absent Sunseed in grain, wards, villages, and political credit, then asks who signs each loss.
encounters.opening_view: A black grain drops into Mirelle Orelle's palm. She weighs it, glances at three open ledgers, and asks who promised the expense without naming its bearer. Above the orchard table hang sheaves marked Loss, Capital, Advantage—wardstones in one, soldiers in another, bright roads and privileges among the rest. Mirelle returns the grain to none of them. It remains in her hand, waiting for a named account.
encounters.content:
## Situation

The Golden Sheaf Exchange occupies an orchard held in perpetual late afternoon. Every obligation spoken beneath its branches appears as a grain of gold on a hanging sheaf. The grain grows heavier with the cost. It turns black when no bearer has been named. The magic reveals no secret price. It only refuses to let generosity remain weightless.

Mirelle lays the black grain from her palm across three open books. It will not settle into Loss, Capital, or Advantage until someone names what is consumed, what remains valuable, and what advantage is being purchased under the name of compensation.

Mirelle opens at three million crowns. Every number is defensible. The total includes reusable wardstones, a reserve returned if no breach occurs, and ten years of exclusive trade privileges valued as though Orison had already granted them. Asked whether all three million would be lost after an uneventful return, she says no. Unasked, she lets the court repeat the larger figure.

> A gift paid by an unconsulted border village is not a gift. It is an invoice delivered by someone with better manners.

Mirelle does not require Orison to pay every line. She requires the coalition to stop calling a line free because the payer is absent.

## What is being priced

The Exchange can produce a complete schedule before the audience ends. Its principal entries are openly available.

- temporary ward lattices around the weakened Dawnward;
- an eastern reserve for Warden Serevin;
- transport and containment for the Sunseed;
- insurance against verified damage to Aurelune;
- delayed seasonal tolls while the passages are unstable;
- expedition provisions and replacement healers; and
- any indemnity, collateral, or trade rights pledged to secure the above.

The schedule can shrink without erasing the risk. Joint custody is cheaper than transfer of ownership. A capped indemnity is cheaper than a general guarantee. A thirteen-day term is more expensive than six days, but the six-day term may make the Orison undertaking fail. Reusable wardstones are capital rather than loss. A reserve posted by several banners requires less profit than one carried by Orelle alone.

Mirelle will discuss each distinction. She does not volunteer the distinction that harms her preferred bargain.

## House Orelle's seal

Orelle can seal through several materially different settlements.

### Orison bears the risk

Orison grants Orelle privileged docks, collection rights on fey-road commerce, and a revenue-backed indemnity for verified Dawnward losses. This is Mirelle's easiest settlement. It finances the security package immediately and burdens a city already facing ruin. Ilyrion opposes any version that can be described as purchasing rescue through dependence.

### Allied guarantors bear the risk

Two or more banners, allied cities, or wealthy estates guarantee a capped sum. Orison remains liable for loss caused by misuse of the Sunseed, but not for ordinary defensive preparations in Aurelune. This route is compatible with Ilyrion and Maelith if the guarantors are named persons rather than Orison's treasury in disguise.

### The coalition shares the risk

Participating banners subscribe to short-term ward bonds. Orelle supplies procurement and accepts a lower return because the undertaking becomes a court-wide public work. This favors a broad concord and makes Eiral more receptive. It also gives every subscribing house a plausible claim to authorship.

### The Crown bears a defined share

The petition records that maintaining the Dawnward is an existing royal obligation. The Crown pays ordinary defense costs; the coalition pays only incremental costs caused by the Sunseed's absence. Caelir will resist the characterization, but he cannot truthfully call all Dawnward expense a foreign liability.

### The political return replaces part of the financial return

Orelle accepts a smaller indemnity in exchange for nonexclusive access to Orison's reconstruction contracts and visible credit for financing the Dawnward. This is less predatory than permanent trade privilege and still changes Orison's post-crisis economy.

## Negotiating the schedule

Mark every line as loss, capital, advantage, or disputed. Mirelle defends each classification.

Useful direct questions include:

- Which items remain Orelle property after the Sunseed returns?
- Which costs would Aurelune incur even if the Sunseed never left?
- Which sums are reserves returned if no breach occurs?
- Which projected values depend on Orelle receiving a monopoly rather than reimbursement?
- What maximum payment would satisfy the house if the Dawnward suffers no verified damage?
- Will Orelle accept several guarantors whose obligations are separate and capped?

Mirelle welcomes a precise audit. She objects when the petitioners call every margin theft. In her view, profit is the part of a promise that remains after enthusiasm has gone home.

## Coalition consequences

### Ilyrion

Saelira can defend a guarantee funded by allied states, court revenue, or participating banners. She will not defend exclusive trade rights extracted from Orison as the price of rescue. A separate reconstruction compact with ordinary competition is acceptable.

### Maelith

Othalan prefers named estates and persons to abstract public credit. His house can become a guarantor, but he will expect the guarantee to strengthen his personal-surety argument elsewhere.

### Serathiel and Serevin

The Exchange can finance both an eastern reserve and substitute warding without giving Serathiel expedition command. It can also finance Serathiel's preferred command structure. Money resolves the resource objection, not the authority dispute.

### Namaris

Pelion can reduce the schedule by defining **compensable loss** as verified, incremental, and unrecovered damage. Orelle accepts the definition if the audit process is funded and the cap is real.

### The Crown

Caelir's evacuation offer appears cheaper because most losses fall on Orison: abandoned property, displaced citizens, and a city left beneath the Pall. Mirelle will confirm that the royal plan does not eliminate cost. It changes whose ledger recognizes it.

## Entries that need names

### Choose the liability base

Indemnify all verified harm, only incremental Dawnward harm, only loss caused by misuse, or a fixed maximum regardless of cause. Each version changes Orelle's price and Namaris's drafting burden.

### Name the payers

Orison, allied guarantors, participating banners, the Crown, or a mixed consortium can bear the obligation. An unnamed promise becomes black grain on the sheaf and does not secure Orelle's seal.

### Authorize procurement

Wardstones and reserve contracts must begin before the fourth court day to support a thirteen-day loan. Authorize procurement before the final vote to make the security package credible, at the cost of money and political capital if the petition fails.

### Decide whether compensation purchases influence

Reimbursement can remain reimbursement, or it can include trade access, reconstruction authority, ceremonial credit, or future fiscal oversight. Mirelle prices these separately. The petitioners must do the same.

## How the Sheaf may leave the exchange

### The bill has names

The petitioners leave with a capped, auditable liability schedule; named payers; procurement authority for the full Dawnward package; and Orelle either declared or ready to seal once the draft incorporates those terms.

### Financing that changes the peace

- Orelle declares immediately in exchange for privileged access to Orison's docks.
- The coalition shares the cost, but every subscribing banner acquires a claim on public credit.
- The Crown pays ordinary defense costs only after the petitioners accept royal co-custody and a narrower undertaking.
- Procurement begins before the coalition is stable, creating sunk costs that royal advocates use to push a compromise.

### The black grain remains

Contest the existence of risk rather than allocating it. Orelle remains open, publishes the three-million-crown figure without the petitioners' classifications, and lets the king cite it as the uncontested price of the loan.

## Carry into the ledgers

- the definition and cap of compensable loss;
- the named guarantors or revenue source;
- whether Orison grants trade or reconstruction privileges;
- which security contracts begin before certification;
- whether the coalition treats ordinary Dawnward defense as a Crown cost; and
- whether Orelle has declared, sealed a side covenant, or merely priced the options.

## On a return

The Exchange remains useful whenever command, term, recall, or custody changes. Mirelle recalculates openly. A more cautious draft lowers some costs and may make the undertaking unusable. A broader coalition lowers the required financial return and raises the number of nobles entitled to say they paid for victory.

reference_links.context: Separates loss, capital, and advantage so security costs can be funded without disguising political purchase as reimbursement.
His Crown-led plan shifts much of the recognized loss onto Orison while keeping ordinary royal defense obligations.
Liability and reconstruction terms can fund rescue or purchase long-lived control over the city.
Evacuation, restoration, and failed rescue place different losses on Orison, Aurelune, and guarantors.
Its absence must be priced in wards, grain, villages, liability, and political credit.

encounters.title: The Amber Quill Archive
encounters.summary: Namaris separates custody from ownership, recall from failure, and elegant language from operative law.
encounters.opening_view: An amber quill writes the precedent before Pelion Namaris welcomes you. A second waits over the adverse index. Cases marked ownership, custody, possession, and use unlock one by one, though their later pages are thicker than their first. Pelion slides the favorable sentence across the table, then turns the index around. He has given you the answer you brought. The next question belongs to your enemy.
encounters.content:
## Situation

The Amber Quill Archive is arranged as a courtroom for litigants not yet born. Shelves rise in rings around a low drafting table. Cite a precedent and an amber quill leaves its case to write the controlling sentence in the air. Ask again and other quills bring the later cases that narrowed it. The first quill never summons the second on its own.

Archivist-Lord Pelion Namaris greets Orison's petitioners with a warning, not a refusal:

> No petition means what its authors remember wanting. It means what a hostile reader can still prove after the authors are dead.

Pelion accepts that necessity may justify the Concord. He has not accepted the petitioners' preferred nouns, boundaries, or consequences. Namaris will seal a text that can survive an audit and a precedent no broader than the court intends.

He lays four old instruments on the table. Their full texts are open to inspection. His advantage is the order in which he teaches them: joint custody before alienation, evacuation before preservation, a feared precedent before the judgments that confined it, personal surety before wardship. Nothing is hidden. A listener who stops after the useful sentence has done Pelion's work for him.

## The adverse index

Demand an **adverse index** for every proposition the draft relies upon. Pelion supplies later precedents, contrary readings, unresolved terms, and the strongest hostile argument. Time buys sight of the king's limiting case before the Conclave.

A direct question closes Namaris's characteristic omission:

> Are there later precedents that limit the rule you have just quoted, and will you identify them before asking us to rely on it?

Pelion answers and then offers the same service against the petitioners' favorite clause. He enjoys the silence that follows.

## Terms the Archive insists on separating

### Ownership, custody, possession, and use

The Crown can retain ownership throughout. Joint custodians may possess the Sunseed, direct its movement, and use it for the named undertaking. A royal custodian can hold a meaningful veto over damage to the relic without receiving authority to redirect the expedition.

### Undertaking and purpose

*Destroy the Pall* is narrow and may allow the expedition to ignore Orison's survival after the central work is done. *Preserve Orison* protects the city but invites argument over whether evacuation counts. *Restore natural day to Orison* best describes the intended result and may require continued custody after the Pall first breaks. *Resist Shadowfell expansion* is strategically broad and alarms Thalan.

### Term and completion

A term ending on completion creates disputes about who decides completion. An absolute date is easy to administer and may expire during failure. Namaris prefers both: completion of the named undertaking, subject to an absolute final day.

### Recall, suspension, and emergency protection

A recall removes the Sunseed from Orison. A suspension halts a particular use. An emergency protection clause permits a custodian to prevent immediate damage without changing the undertaking. Courtiers call all three **recall** whenever the blur gives them more authority than the exact noun would.

### Return

Physical delivery to Aurelune leaves replanting beneath the throne and restoration of the Dawnward unfinished. The petition must state which act discharges custody and which obligations survive afterward.

### Recognition and command

Calling Orison a treaty partner does not by itself give its envoy operational authority. Giving a mortal co-custodian authority does not by itself protect Orison's civil government. If the coalition wants both, both must be written.

## House Namaris's seal

Namaris can support through any of three principal routes.
