### The narrow instrument

The petition names the Sunseed, the Pall, Orison, a maximum term, exact custodians, a bounded recall process, an audit, and a relic-specific sunset. It expressly denies a general right to other Crown treasures. This route pleases Thalan and may confine Ilyrion's broader recognition goals to a side compact.

### The reviewed instrument

The court adopts workable language now and schedules a formal constitutional review after the crisis. Audit reports, command disputes, and the actual effect on the Dawnward become part of the record. Namaris accepts slightly broader language because it will not harden into unexamined custom.

### The integrated concord

Eight or more banners adopt a central petition plus coordinated side covenants for recognition, surety, financing, command detail, public credit, and post-crisis review. Namaris accepts the complexity if the central instrument states which covenant yields when terms conflict.

Pelion will not seal a rhetorical compromise that relies on every house continuing to interpret the same phrase differently.

## Drafting exercises

The Archive offers the petitioners clauses with their consequences visible.

### A mortal refusal right

A mortal co-custodian may refuse any change of undertaking, transfer of the Sunseed to a new destination, or use against Orison's civil authorities. The refusal does not block ordinary tactical command within the agreed undertaking. This protects Orison without creating an unworkable unanimity rule.

### A personal bond without wardship

Three named estates guarantee return and verified misuse. No person is detained and no polity becomes subordinate. Maelith receives durable personal answerability; Ilyrion preserves sovereign standing.

### A limited precedence ruling

The petition may recognize Vaudren's ceremonial precedence for the Sunseed procession without deciding general rank between Vaudren and Maelith. The public satisfaction is real and bounded.

### Necessity and sunset

The recitals may find that the Pall threatens Orison, the natural cycle, and Aurelune's strategic frontier, while the operative article states that the instrument may not be cited beyond the Sunseed and the named emergency after its review date.

### Correctable defects

A defect discovered before certification does not require restarting if the undertaking remains the same and every materially affected banner reaffirms. An amendment to custody, command, liability, recall, or return is normally material. A corrected title or cross-reference is not.

## Truthful pressure

Pelion rarely says a proposed clause is impossible. He says that no approved precedent supports it, meaning none in the set he has chosen to call approved. He says a term has always meant one thing, meaning in the cases that use that exact capitalized term. He answers the legal effect and lets the petitioners mistake it for the likely political result.

Characters trained in law or diplomacy recognize the technique. The useful response is not to catch him in dishonesty. It is to request the adverse index, distinguish the proposition, or make him state the strongest contrary reading in the record.

## Drafting choices that cannot remain implied

### Choose the undertaking sentence

The Archive can produce several valid versions. The choice determines whether evacuation, partial daylight, military redirection, or continued custody can count as success.

### Decide what belongs in the petition

Custody, term, command authority, recall, liability, and return must be central. Recognition, fosterage, finance, credit, audit detail, and deployment schedules may sit in side covenants. Keeping a promise outside the central text can preserve clarity and weaken enforcement.

### Commission an adverse index

Spend time now to expose the king's strongest legal arguments before the Conclave. Skipping the index accelerates drafting and leaves the royal counter-coalition more room.

### Offer review or closure

A formal post-crisis review gives reformers a later forum and conservatives a mechanism for limiting precedent. An express nonprecedential clause is faster and may be politically insufficient for either side.

## How the Quill may leave the index

### A text hostile readers can survive

The petitioners leave with a workable clause set, a list of material amendments that would release seals, a lawful architecture for side covenants, and Namaris either declared or conditionally ready to seal after final review.

### Precision that narrows the victory

- The petition becomes narrow enough for Thalan and Namaris but moves Ilyrion's recognition goals into a later compact.
- The court schedules a constitutional review, giving Aven and reformers a durable forum while prolonging the dispute after Orison is saved.
- The petitioners commission a complete adverse index and lose a public appointment elsewhere.
- The text preserves every bargain through elaborate cross-references that only Namaris can administer quickly.

### Elegant language, no operative meaning

Ask Pelion to make the language **good enough** without naming which risks it accepts. He produces a legally valid minimal draft that preserves Crown ownership, royal command, a six-day term, and evacuation as sufficient preservation. Nothing in it is false or defective. It is the king's preferred outcome in competent prose.

## Enter in the adverse index

- the exact undertaking sentence;
- the distinction among title, custody, possession, and use;
- which terms sit in side covenants;
- the audit, sunset, and review structure;
- the mortal co-custodian's refusal rights;
- the list of amendments deemed material; and
- whether an adverse index has already exposed the Crown's strongest legal case.

## On a return

Every substantial political compromise eventually returns to the Archive. Pelion becomes more useful as the coalition grows and more dangerous when the petitioners ask him to reconcile promises the coalition has never made compatible.

reference_links.context: Tests every operative noun against precedent, later limitation, auditability, and the rule a hostile court might cite.
Its lawful force depends on exact custody, command, term, recall, liability, return, and precedent language.
Its passage right and legal limits must not be mistaken for a general alliance or sovereign-status judgment.
The undertaking must distinguish restoring the city from evacuating its people or merely breaking the Pall.
The named undertaking must say whether success means breaking the siege-work, restoring day, or preserving the city.

encounters.title: The Hall of First Frost
encounters.summary: Thalan asks what necessity permits today without becoming a standing license against the Crown tomorrow.
encounters.opening_view: Ice gathers beneath Eirath Thalan's words and makes an old compelled loan visible underfoot: late return, fallen keep, unpaid taxes, a later petition refused. The lines touch, separate, and touch again as she names them. Fresh frost leaves spaces for substitute wards, an outside date, measured failure. Eirath looks down through three generations. "Orison may die. Tell me what that permits—and what it does not."
encounters.content:
## Situation

The Hall of First Frost is paved in clear ice that thickens whenever a constitutional claim is spoken. Each argument becomes another layer beneath the floor. Older claims remain visible, distorted by everything said above them and never quite gone.

Duchess Eirath Thalan waits over the record of every compelled royal loan. She accepts the Pall, the measurements, and Orison's peril. She disputes the move from catastrophe to constitutional necessity.

Eirath recites the Briar Compulsion: a late return, a fallen keep, taxes refused, an ambitious later citation, a king who died unreconciled with his court. Every event belongs in the history. She begins without sorting cause from coincidence or opportunism. The oath does not sort it for her.

A direct question makes her do so:

> Which of those consequences do you claim were caused by the compelled custody rather than by the war already underway?

The keep might have fallen regardless. The tax refusal was opportunistic. The later citation failed. Eirath concedes each point and keeps the one she means: a lawful victory can still leave a wound between Crown and court, and wounds become precedent when no one names them.

## Thalan's constitutional case

House Thalan asks Orison's petitioners to satisfy four propositions.

### The necessity belongs partly to Aurelune

Sympathy for a foreign city is not enough. The petition must explain why the Pall threatens the natural cycle, Aurelune's treaties, or the eastern balance against the Shadowfell. Serevin's border assessment and Ilyrion's alliance claim can both support this finding for different reasons.

### The instrument remains exceptional

The Sunseed, the Pall, Orison, and the maximum term must be named. The court should not create a general doctrine that seven banners may seize any useful Crown relic whenever a foreign emergency is grave.

### The Crown retains a meaningful office

Title alone is insufficient if every royal custodian is ceremonial. Eirath accepts royal co-custody, authority to prevent damage to the Sunseed, participation in the recall process, and the right to state a dissenting constitutional rationale in the final instrument.

### Victory is not written as humiliation

The petition may compel Caelir. It need not describe him as faithless, defeated, or unworthy of trust. Thalan treats language as institutional action. A preamble celebrating the court's triumph can lose her seal even when the operative clauses are cautious.

## Routes to Thalan's seal

### Narrow necessity

Adopt a recital that the Pall threatens Orison, the cycle of seasons, and Aurelune's eastern security; limits custody to thirteen days or completion; preserves Crown title and co-custody; and includes a relic-specific sunset. This is Thalan's direct route.

### Voluntary royal joinder

Assemble seven seals on acceptable terms and offers Caelir a dignified way to join the petition. If he joins, Eirath can tolerate broader recognition or command provisions because the Crown has consented to them rather than suffered them all by compulsion. The king need not endorse the court's reasoning.

### Emergency action followed by full review

The petition remains narrow, while a scheduled constitutional convention later addresses Orison's status, adopted heirs, and the future scope of the Concord. Ilyrion and Aven receive a real forum rather than an unenforceable promise. Thalan refuses to decide those matters through a seven-day crisis.

### A more cautious petition

A six-day term, stronger royal control, or a restrictive recall article can secure Thalan quickly. Each may make the rescue less usable. Eirath does not treat operational failure as a constitutional virtue, but she will not conceal the tradeoff.

## The necessity record

Build the record in the hall. Eirath asks each factual proposition to be stated without rhetorical surplus.

- At moonrise after Court Day Seven, the Pall closes the Lantern Road and becomes self-sustaining.
- The noon-market stone and Dawnward test show that the Sunseed can restore natural day to Orison.
- Removing it weakens but does not extinguish the Dawnward.
- The Gloam Host can observe that weakness.
- Substitute wards and reserves can reduce the risk.
- The Crown's evacuation plan preserves some people and not the city.
- No other known relic can accomplish the same undertaking within the time available.

The last proposition is not a hidden discovery. Caelir and every house accept it. The dispute concerns the legal and moral conclusion drawn from it.

## Recall and emergency power

Eirath opposes unilateral recall by Serevin or the Crown. She will accept a defined breach trigger confirmed by multiple custodians. She also accepts immediate suspension of a use that would visibly damage the Sunseed, provided suspension cannot be converted into a change of undertaking.

This compromise helps Serevin, Namaris, and Eiral. It frustrates any house seeking complete discretion.

## Seasonal balance

The Hall preserves the oldest surviving Concord text. It states the four-season requirement separately from the seven-seal count. Eirath will not entertain an argument that urgency waives the distinction. The Ashen Bough and Eiral may increase the total and cannot replace a missing seasonal seal.

## Claims that need owners

### Choose the theory of necessity

Ground necessity in alliance, natural order, common defense, or some combination. A broad theory attracts Ilyrion and Eiral. A narrow military theory attracts Serevin and Serathiel. The chosen theory will be quoted at the Conclave.

### Preserve or minimize royal authority

Offer royal title, co-custody, damage prevention, recall participation, and public framing separately. Decide which powers are operative and which are courteous.

### Separate reform from rescue

Place recognition and inheritance reform in side covenants or a scheduled later convention. Doing so makes Thalan easier and asks reformers to trust a future proceeding.

### Invite royal joinder

Offering Caelir a path into the final text may strengthen the outcome. It also gives him leverage to demand revisions after the coalition has assembled seven seals.

## How First Frost may join the season call

### Necessity without a general license

Thalan accepts a stated theory of necessity, the Crown retains a meaningful but bounded role, and the petition gains a sunset or review structure. Eirath becomes open to sealing rather than merely ceasing opposition.

### Restraint that limits the rescue

- Recognition reform moves to a later convention sponsored now by named banners.
- The king receives a purpose-limited veto over damage and redirection.
- The petitioners promise not to characterize the result as a defeat for the Crown, limiting Vaudren's appetite for public triumph.
- The term shortens unless the security package is fully funded.

### Compassion without a constitutional finding

Argue only that saving Orison is morally right and treats constitutional caution as cowardice. Thalan remains opposed, supplies the king with a disciplined public argument, and makes any Winter coalition depend on Serevin alone.

## Freeze into the record

- the petition's theory of necessity;
- the scope of the relic-specific sunset;
- the Crown's retained powers;
- whether reform is inside the emergency instrument or calendared later;
- whether Caelir has been offered voluntary joinder; and
- the exact objective standard for recall or emergency suspension.

## On a return

Thalan revisits her support whenever the undertaking expands, the term lengthens, or the final rhetoric changes. She is easier to win than to keep if the coalition treats cautious language as disposable once her Winter seal is secured.

reference_links.context: Permits emergency compulsion without erasing the Crown's continuing interest or making the relic ordinary public property.
His compelled duty, voluntary joinder, and royal dignity define how narrow constitutional restraint can remain usable.
Makes constitutional recall concrete by demanding an observable breach and lawful verification rather than discretionary fear.
Its real emergency supports necessity without itself proving that every compelled-loan precedent is sound.
The compelled loan tests how narrowly emergency necessity can govern a royal trust.

encounters.title: The Silent Fir Lodge
encounters.summary: Serevin releases Winter only when the eastern marches receive troops, warding, and a recall rule that can be measured.
encounters.opening_view: Caldus Serevin does not greet you. A living wall drops one silver needle onto the eastern map, then another. Most lie in the old rings of musters, funerals, patrols. Three do not: scouts at Half-Light, siege beasts west of the valley, fires out of season. Beside them wait an unsigned ward contract, a reserve order, and a recall clause whose trigger is still blank.
encounters.content:
## Situation

The Silent Fir Lodge stands at the eastern edge of the royal demesne. Its walls are living trunks cut with rings marking every recorded movement of the Gloam Host for two centuries. Fresh silver needles cross a relief map as reports arrive. Warden Caldus Serevin has placed every current report on the table before Orison's petitioners enter.

All of them describe movement. Some are musters, funerary marches, supply rotations, or patrols answering Aurelune's own concentration of force. Three are wrong for the season: scouts near the Half-Light Causeway, siege beasts moved one valley west, and repeated signal fires beyond the usual calendar.

Caldus does not claim to know that invasion is coming. He claims that an intelligent enemy can see the Dawnward thin and that the marches cannot be made to carry Orison's rescue without orders, troops, and a lawful trigger.

His opening sentence is true and weighted:

> Every eastern report describes movement.

The useful question is not whether he lied. It is which movement exceeds the baseline, which he judges hostile, and what authority he wants before either judgment can be tested.

## The actual border risk

The Dawnward does three things while the Sunseed remains beneath the throne.

- It obscures the timing of seasonal passages through the eastern passes.
- It strengthens six ward stations against shadow creatures and siege magic.
- It lets Serevin move a reserve between the Half-Light Causeway and the Fir March in hours rather than days.

Removing the Sunseed weakens all three. It does not open the border. The Gloam Host must still choose to attack, concentrate forces, and cross defended ground. A credible replacement package makes an opportunistic invasion expensive enough that Caldus can recommend the loan.

## The replacement package

Serevin divides the solution into four separable obligations.

### Substitute warding

Six portable wardstones can maintain the most important stations for thirteen days. Orelle can finance them. The stones do not preserve the seasonal passages and remain valuable property after the crisis.

### Eastern reserve

Serathiel can assign troops to the Half-Light Causeway under Serevin's local command. This answers the border need without granting the marshal command of the Orison expedition. Serathiel may demand credit or a stronger voice elsewhere in exchange.

### Allied deployment

Orison's allies can send troops directly. Those troops will not reach Orison in time for the central expedition if they are diverted east. Ilyrion accepts the deployment only if it is requested as allied burden sharing rather than imposed as tribute.

### Recall procedure

If an actual border breach occurs, Aurelune needs authority to protect itself. Caldus's preferred language lets him recall the Sunseed upon his own certified finding. He will accept less unilateral alternatives if they can act quickly.

## Recall models

### Unilateral recall

Serevin declares a breach and orders immediate return. This is fastest and can doom Orison on evidence no other custodian has reviewed.

### Objective trigger

The petition defines a breach through observable conditions: an organized hostile force crosses the ward line, two stations fail or are bypassed, and the eastern reserve cannot contain the advance. Serevin certifies the facts; the recall follows automatically. Namaris and Thalan prefer this model.

### Recall panel

Serevin presents the evidence to a royal custodian and an expedition custodian. Two of three may recall. Eiral can chair communications and resolve whether the trigger has been met. This is slower and more governable.

### Emergency suspension

Serevin may order the Sunseed held ready for return for a fixed number of hours while evidence is confirmed. The expedition loses time but not necessarily the undertaking. This route is useful when reports are serious and incomplete.

### Reinforcement before recall

The security covenant commits additional troops or ward power automatically when defined warning signs appear. Recall becomes the final step rather than the first.

Caldus accepts that **movement** cannot itself be the trigger. He insists that a plan with no response to genuine invasion is not a plan.

## House Serevin's seal

Serevin can support through several combinations.

- substitute wards plus an eastern reserve and an objective recall trigger;
- a shorter term plus a smaller reserve and a recall panel;
- allied troops under Serevin command with no unilateral recall;
- a fully funded Dawnward package with emergency suspension rather than recall; or
- Caelir's voluntary joinder, if the king assumes responsibility for reinforcing the marches.

The house's red line is not lack of perfect safety. It is making the eastern border absorb the risk without resources or lawful authority.

## Coalition consequences

### Serathiel

Putting the reserve under Serevin command allows Ysandre to yield expedition command while still claiming military success. Putting all forces under Serathiel may win Summer support and lose Serevin's trust.

### Orelle

The ward package can be translated into measurable performance, duration, and delivery terms. Orelle finances it as a bounded contract rather than an unlimited guarantee.

### Thalan

A sober record of both Orison's danger and Aurelune's exposure strengthens the necessity finding. Exaggerating the Gloam Host's present intent weakens Thalan's confidence in the whole petition.

### Eiral

A multi-party recall mechanism demonstrates governability. A unilateral power held by a house already opposed to the loan makes Eiral fear that the coalition cannot carry out what it authorizes.

### The Crown

Caelir proposes a six-day term as the cleanest answer to border risk. Caldus agrees that six days is safer for Aurelune and states that it may be operationally insufficient for Orison. The offer is a real loan structured to place the risk of delay on the city being rescued.

## Orders the border needs

### Adopt the threat baseline

Ask Caldus to sign a schedule separating ordinary movement, warning signs, and actual breach conditions. This limits later alarmism and also binds the expedition to act when the defined signs occur.

### Allocate troops

Forces assigned east cannot simultaneously escort the Sunseed, hold Orison's perimeter, or operate the evacuation gates. The adventurers choose where scarcity falls.

### Choose the recall model

Speed, evidence, and shared authority cannot all be maximized. The chosen model will become one of the petition's most dangerous clauses.

### Fund the package

Wardstones and reserve orders require Orelle or another guarantor. A promise to fund them later does not move a single soldier before the Dawnward weakens.

## How the Fir may leave the watch

### A defended march and a usable Sunseed

Secure a signed baseline, a funded replacement package, a named eastern commander, and a recall mechanism that answers invasion without allowing ordinary movement to terminate the undertaking.

### Security purchased with flexibility

- Allied troops defend Aurelune instead of accompanying the expedition to Orison.
- Serevin yields unilateral recall only after gaining local command over Serathiel's reserve.
- The petitioners accept an emergency suspension that may consume crucial hours at the Pall.
- The term shortens because the coalition declines to fund all six wardstones.

### Alarm retains the recall power

Dismiss the border risk as a pretext. Caldus remains opposed, publishes the complete reports without a shared baseline, and allows the king to describe the petition as a plan that asks the marches to trust optimism.

## Enter in the watch record

- the signed threat baseline;
- the number and funding of substitute wardstones;
- the size, source, and commander of the eastern reserve;
- the objective warning and breach conditions;
- the recall or suspension mechanism; and
- which forces are no longer available for Orison.

## On a return

The Lodge changes whenever the term, Dawnward package, or Gloam Host posture changes. Caldus does not invent new threats to reopen a bargain. He does use every genuine movement to test whether the coalition still accepts the risk it asked him to bear.

reference_links.context: Controls the border-defense problem, the seasonal baseline, and any authority assigned to respond to an actual breach.
Her expedition command can be separated from Serevin's border command without abandoning coherent authority.
Can finance substitute wards and reserves, but ownership, return, and profit must remain explicit.
His six-day expedition is the Crown's cleanest border-risk answer and a genuine but shorter rescue.
A measurable border breach may justify recall, but unilateral recall could doom Orison.

encounters.title: The Twilight Laurel Apartments
encounters.summary: Theron separates public duty from House Eiral's seal and tests whether the coalition can govern its own contradictions.
encounters.opening_view: Theron Eiral turns one ring as he crosses the doorway. At the black desk wait seven seal lines, four seasonal boxes, and the Chamberlain's stamp. At the supper table, ten cups stand beneath a laurel half green and half gold; one belongs to the Crown. His face does not alter. "You may address my office," he says, "or my house. You may not pretend they are the same."
encounters.content:
## Situation

The Twilight Laurel Apartments divide one room with an open doorway. The black desk holds the court calendar and certification seal; the supper table stands beneath a laurel half green and half gold. Theron turns one ring at the threshold, and courtiers quote one room in the other whenever confusion serves them.

He will not prevent the petitioners from separating the interviews. He will notice whether they bother.

## The official interview

At the black desk, Theron answers questions of law and calendar.

- He must certify a petition that satisfies the Concord.
- He must identify contradictions rather than cure them by favorable interpretation.
- He may order hearings, corrective recesses, and the sequence of public business.
- He may not require an eighth seal, royal assent, or House Eiral's political approval.

His habitual phrase is, “The Chamberlain has taken no position.” It can remain true while House Eiral bargains through every supper invitation in the palace. The binding question is not whether the Chamberlain approves. It is what the rules require him to do next.

## The House Eiral interview

At the laurel table, Theron sets an eighth cup beside the king's and asks what the victors expect everyone to call the settlement ten years hence. House Eiral wants more than validity: it wants a court that can execute the result without naming humiliation concord.

The house prefers eight banners, or seven with Caelir's voluntary joinder. It wants one public purpose, a neutral method for conflicts among custodians, and terms the king can obey without surrendering the idea that the Sunseed was his trust to guard.

Theron will not threaten certification. He does not need to. The house can withhold its banner, its supper table, and the language by which half the court later describes the outcome.

## Routes to Eiral's seal

### Eight-banner concord

Eight or more banners accept a shared public purpose, a neutral chair, and a conflict process. Eiral will normally seal such a petition even if Caelir remains opposed. Breadth makes withdrawal and retaliation harder.

### Seven banners plus royal joinder

A legal majority assembles first and then offers Caelir defined co-custody, public dignity, and a place in the final declaration. If he joins voluntarily, Eiral treats the settlement as governable despite its narrow count.

### Seven banners with institutional safeguards

A bare majority can still win Eiral if the petition includes a neutral chair, a rapid dispute mechanism, objective recall triggers, and a shared public statement adopted at the Masque. This route requires more exact agreement than merely finding an eighth vote.

### Neutral chair without Eiral's seal

Theron may chair the undertaking or its recall panel while House Eiral remains unsealed. The service improves governability and certification but does not add a vote. Eiral will not let the petitioners describe official service as political support.

## Shared purpose

The house offers several public formulations.

- **To preserve Orison as a free city beneath its natural sky and to protect Aurelune during the Sunseed's absence.** This is broad, balanced, and attractive to Ilyrion, Serevin, and Thalan.
- **To repel Shadowfell expansion through a joint defense of both realms.** This is militarily coherent and gives Serathiel more authority.
- **To execute the Crown's mercy toward Orison while maintaining royal custody.** This favors Caelir and Maelith and weakens the independent coalition.
- **To restore natural day without determining any broader political relation.** This is narrow enough for Thalan and Namaris and may disappoint reformers.

A shared purpose is not decoration. Eiral will use it to interpret command disputes and proposed amendments.

## Royal dignity

Theron distinguishes dignity that changes nothing from dignity that stabilizes the settlement.

Operative protections include:

- Crown title and one royal co-custodian;
- authority to prevent physical damage or unauthorized redirection;
- a right to present the Crown's constitutional dissent in the instrument;
- public language describing the result as concord after lawful disagreement; and
- a place for Caelir in the departure ceremony whether or not he seals.

A jeweled chair, first procession, or flattering title may satisfy Vaudren and does not by itself satisfy Thalan or Eiral.

## The king's counter-coalition

Theron expects Caelir to offer different houses different parts of the same narrow settlement: exclusive royal command to Serathiel, personal custody to Maelith, short duration to Serevin and Thalan, public credit to Vaudren, and compensation to Orelle. Every offer can be true and compatible with the others. Together they replace the petitioning coalition with a royal expedition.

Eiral's answer is not proving the king dishonest. It is making each banner state whether its support depends on the central shared purpose or only on the private benefit it has been offered.

## Decisions across the doorway

### Separate office from house

Request an official defect review now and a political interview later, or conduct both in sequence. Blending them is faster and makes later quotations dangerous.

### Choose the coalition standard

Seek eight seals, seven plus the king, or seven with stronger institutions. The choice affects how much Eiral demands and how the Masque should be staged.

### Name a neutral chair

Theron, Namaris, a mortal co-custodian, or a rotating panel can resolve disputes. Every chair brings a different bias and source of legitimacy.

### Fix the public purpose

A statement adopted before final drafting can hold the coalition together. It can also release houses whose private bargains no longer fit what they publicly affirmed.

### Spend calendar time

Saving the Ashen Bough hearing preserves a possible vote. Advancing a draft review stabilizes existing declarations. Keeping every private appointment maximizes bargaining and risks arriving at the petition chamber with incompatible promises.

## How the Laurel may turn either ring

### Validity and governability separated cleanly

Obtain a clean official checklist, a workable calendar, a stated route to House Eiral's seal, and a shared-purpose formula capable of surviving the Masque. Theron agrees to chair or certify without pretending those acts are the same.

### An eighth seal bought with ownership

- The petitioners secure Eiral by seeking eight seals and accepting neutral public credit.
- The Ashen Bough hearing displaces another public audience.
- Caelir receives a dignified path into the petition and uses it to demand late revisions.
- A neutral chair gains genuine authority over command and recall disputes.

### Office and banner left confused

Repeatedly cites Theron's official duties as proof of House Eiral's support. He corrects the record beneath the Canopy, remains neutral as a banner-holder, and performs every official duty with exact restraint.

## Record which ring was turned

- the official defect checklist and remaining calendar;
- the coalition standard required for Eiral's seal;
- the shared public purpose;
- the neutral chair or conflict mechanism;
- the Crown's operative dignity protections;
- whether the Ashen Bough hearing remains timely; and
- which statements were made in Theron's official and political capacities.

## On a return

The Apartments test whether a growing coalition can still govern. Theron requires every contradiction to have an acknowledged decision-maker, not two nobles waiting for the other to yield.

reference_links.context: Makes the distinction between Theron's public office and House Eiral's political bargain explicit.
Separates Theron's certification duty from House Eiral's political seal and the king's later joinder.
Eiral tests whether a lawful coalition can give him a governable role without making royal assent the source of validity.

encounters.title: The Ashen Bough Hearing
encounters.summary: A succession hearing may supply an eighth banner, but only by making the coalition own the doctrine that seats it.
encounters.opening_view: Theron names one duty Vaelor Avarre left behind. An ember leaf opens above the empty Ashen chair, hangs between Mirath's marshal's baton and Aven Tal's sealed adoption, then falls when neither claimant owns it. Advocates begin arranging a military regency, a child's inheritance, and a term ending with the Sunseed's return. The gray bough waits for someone to claim tomorrow morning.
encounters.content:
## Situation

The Ashen Bough hangs above an empty chair in a round court open to the evening sky. Its gray branches kindle an ember-colored leaf for each recognized obligation of House Avarre; a leaf falls when that obligation has no owner.

Theron places three instruments beneath the branch: Vaelor's blood genealogy, Mirath's three regency commissions, and Aven Tal's sealed adoption. The adoption names Aven child for household, estate, and personal obligations; no presentation to the Crown names him bearer of the Great Banner. Mirath points to the missing public act. Aven points to duties the court already enforces. An ember leaf falls over each obligation neither claimant will concede.

Mirath denies that Aven is Vaelor's **natural heir**. Aven denies that Mirath was named **successor**. Neither statement touches the other's claim.

The court may seat either one, impose a bounded regency, divide duties without a vote, or leave the chair empty. The danger is not a hidden correct answer. It is an answer the court will use long after Orison's sky has returned.

## Procedure

Theron marks two thresholds on the hearing slate: six of the nine sitting banners, including two seasons, for a final succession judgment; five for a regency limited to the Sunseed undertaking. Fewer leaves the chair empty. The king may speak and bargain but casts no Great Banner vote.

The petitioners vote only if they already represent a banner. Otherwise the emergency petition gives them standing to question the claimants, broker a remedy, recruit the required houses, and decide whether the tenth vote is worth the doctrine that creates it.

## Lady Mirath Avarre

Mirath argues that a Great Banner is a public office before it is property. Vaelor's private adoption transferred household obligations and estate rights. It did not give the court a known bearer able to command troops, answer ancient compacts, or defend the seasonal order.

Her political position is martial but not merely Serathiel's.

- She will seal a petition with coherent expedition command and real eastern defense.
- She accepts divided command if one officer has authority during immediate danger.
- She supports a temporary regency that ends when the Sunseed returns and does not brand Aven's adoption invalid.
- She opposes language treating every adopted heir as automatically entitled to a public banner without court acknowledgment.

Mirath's truthful deception lies in public-law nouns. She speaks of **the banner's heir** when she means the person entitled to its office, then lets listeners hear **Vaelor's heir** in every respect.

## Aven Tal

Aven argues that Aurelune cannot celebrate chosen kinship in private law and deny it at the point where rank becomes consequential. Vaelor bound him to the house's debts, ancestral duties, and mourning rites. The court should not accept those burdens and refuse the banner because the chosen child was mortal-born.

His political position is reformist but not identical to Ilyrion's.

- He will seal a petition naming Orison a political partner and giving a mortal co-custodian meaningful authority.
- He does not require the emergency petition to establish a general right of mortal inheritance.
- He can accept a temporary Mirath regency if his adoption remains valid, his ultimate claim is calendared for full judgment, and the current petition does not subordinate Orison.
- He opposes any settlement stating that only blood can carry a Great Banner.

Aven's truthful deception lies in private-law nouns. He calls himself Vaelor's **heir** without adding that the court has never decided whether the term carries the public office.

## Lawful outcomes

### Seat Mirath as banner-holder

Six banners recognize blood continuity and public capacity as sufficient. Mirath receives the tenth vote and can seal the Sunseed petition. Serathiel and Maelith are strengthened. Ilyrion and Aven demand language making clear that adoption itself remains valid.

### Seat Aven as banner-holder

Six banners hold that the sealed adoption carries the house's public obligations. Aven receives the tenth vote and favors Orison's equality. Ilyrion is strengthened. Maelith and Thalan seek language limiting the precedent to a fully executed adoption by a reigning banner-holder.

### Appoint Mirath as emergency regent

Five banners appoint Mirath only through return of the Sunseed or expiration of the petition. She may cast the Ashen Bough during that term. Aven's inheritance claim remains undecided and receives a scheduled hearing afterward. This is Maelith and Thalan's easiest compromise.

Aven accepts only if the order does not call Mirath **heir**, preserves the adoption's validity, and prevents the emergency from becoming indefinite.

### Appoint a conditional regency

Mirath becomes regent and may cast the banner only on the Sunseed petition and associated security covenants. She cannot use the office to alter the estate or succession record. This is narrower and makes the Ashen Bough almost a single-purpose vote.

A scope-limited regency must state how later drafting affects its authority. Corrections that preserve the named undertaking, authorized covenants, and outside term remain within the order. A material amendment may release the Ashen seal and require Mirath to reaffirm. A changed undertaking, a new use of the Sunseed, or a term extending beyond the regency requires renewed authority from the succession court before the banner can seal again.

### Establish joint stewardship

Mirath commands the house's troops; Aven administers the estate and personal obligations. Neither may cast the banner until the full succession judgment. This preserves both claims, reduces immediate conflict, and leaves the coalition with only nine possible votes.

### Leave the seat vacant

The court declines to exploit a succession crisis for the petition's convenience. Neither claimant becomes an enemy merely because the petitioners choose another route to seven seals. The unresolved doctrine remains for later.

## Public examination

Require each claimant to state the exact conditions under which they would cast the banner. Those answers are declarations rather than seals. They become part of the hearing record and make later withdrawal politically expensive.

Useful questions include:

- Do you deny the validity of the adoption instrument, or only its power to transfer the banner?
- Would you accept an emergency regency that expressly preserves the later claim?
- Which command structure is sufficient for your seal, and which merely preferable?
- Does Orison's equality need to appear in the central petition, or may a guaranteed side compact suffice?
- Will you support the Sunseed undertaking if the court recognizes the other claimant?

The last question matters. Mirath may support the petition through military assistance even if Aven is seated. Aven may support Orison's petitioners and Ilyrion even if Mirath becomes regent. The succession result does not have to reduce either person to a defeated obstacle.

## Coalition effects

### Maelith

Othalan supports a bounded Mirath regency because it supplies a named noble guarantor without deciding inheritance under pressure. He can also accept Aven if a limiting doctrine preserves formal acknowledgment for future banners.

### Serathiel

Mirath's seal strengthens a martial coalition. Aven can still accept coherent command if a mortal custodian retains authority over changes to the undertaking.

### Ilyrion

Aven's seating is a public victory for chosen kinship and mortal standing. Saelira can tolerate Mirath's regency if the order preserves Aven's adoption and the petition recognizes Orison independently.

### Thalan

Eirath prefers an emergency regency to a permanent doctrinal judgment made because the petitioners want one more vote. She can support either final claimant after full argument and dislikes pretending urgency has answered the larger question.

### Eiral

House Eiral supports any remedy adopted through its stated threshold, written without insulting the losing claim, and integrated into a governable coalition. A claimant seated by a razor-thin arrangement of immediate beneficiaries makes the Ashen Bough a liability rather than a stabilizing eighth vote.

## Judgments the petitioners must choose to own

### Decide whether the tenth vote is needed

Already have a plausible route to seven. Pursuing the hearing can broaden the coalition, reshape it, or consume the time needed to reconcile existing bargains.

### Choose final judgment or emergency relief

A final decision creates durable law and requires six banners. A regency is easier, narrower, and vulnerable to the charge that the petitioners manufactured a temporary voter.

### Broker terms between the claimants

Preserve Aven's adoption, limit Mirath's office, schedule later judgment, divide household functions, and define whether the banner may vote on matters beyond the Sunseed.

### Demand public coalition prices

Requiring exact declarations helps at the Masque and gives the king less room to buy the eventual bearer privately. It also binds the petitioners to treat the claimant's stated ground seriously.

## How the hearing may close

### A lawful bearer with a bounded doctrine

The court adopts a clear lawful remedy, the Ashen Bough becomes either a usable vote or an intentionally unavailable one, and neither claimant is falsely declared fraudulent. The result creates an explicit alignment rather than a hidden resentment.

### A vote that outlives the emergency

- Mirath becomes regent and the petition adopts a stronger military package.
- Aven is seated and the court accepts a limiting inheritance doctrine to hold Thalan and Maelith.
- The hearing preserves both claims but consumes a public appointment and yields no vote.
- The Ashen Bough can vote only on the Sunseed petition, making later amendments especially sensitive.

### The branch remains unowned

Treat the hearing as a search for the real heir and accuse one claimant of lying. Both answer the accusation precisely, the court closes ranks around its lawful ambiguity, and the seat remains vacant for lack of a proposed remedy.

## Enter in the succession record

- whether the Ashen Bough is occupied and by whom;
- whether the result is final succession or temporary regency;
- the doctrine stated about adoption, blood, acknowledgment, and public office;
- the scope and end date of any regent's voting authority;
- each claimant's public condition for supporting the Sunseed petition; and
- which houses spent influence to produce the result.

## On a return

The hearing may be reopened only for a material breach of the adopted order or after the emergency term ends. Both claimants remain political actors regardless of who holds the banner. Judgment does not remove the losing claimant from court.

reference_links.context: Reads the uncontested succession record and keeps the hearing within the court calendar.
Its vacant office, paired claims, thresholds, and scope-limited remedies determine whether a tenth vote exists without deciding hidden truth.

encounters.title: The Masque of Plain Faces
encounters.summary: Oath-mirrors give private conditions authors and let every abandoned promise keep its witness until dawn.
encounters.opening_view: The oath-mirror repeats a courtier's declaration before she lowers her clear mask. It preserves her posture, her witnesses, and the question she declined. Four seasonal doors admit banners in order; Caelir enters barefaced. Servants carry separate tablets for recognition, surety, credit, troops, and precedence. Nothing spoken is yet a seal. By dawn, every promise abandoned here will still possess its author's name.
encounters.content:
## Situation

The Masque of Plain Faces opens on the fourth evening in a gallery joined to all four seasonal gardens. Every guest wears clear glass. Etiquette requires each speaker to address the mask rather than the face behind it, allowing a courtier to insist—truthfully—that a remark was made to an office, a house, or a public role and not to the person who heard it.

Oath-mirrors stand on silver tripods. When a recognized voice makes a formal declaration, the nearest mirror repeats the exact words once and keeps their reflection until dawn. It records language, posture, witnesses, and the questions declined. It cannot record intent.

The Masque is where private terms acquire owners. A house may declare support, name a sufficient condition, subscribe to a side covenant, challenge another house's account, or offer a rival settlement. No declaration is a seal. Every declaration gives the court a sentence to place beside a later withdrawal.

King Caelir attends barefaced. Caelir attends barefaced. The Crown is legally never masked.

## What the Masque changes

Before the Masque, a house can give each rival a different true fragment. A witnessed declaration forces the fragments to coexist in public.

Use the event to:

- turn negotiated terms into declarations other houses can rely upon;
- establish a shared purpose broad enough for Eiral without erasing each house's separate ground;
- resolve Vaudren's demand for public satisfaction;
- replace Maelith's preferred fosterage with a witnessed personal bond;
- assemble Orelle's guarantor consortium and Serevin's border package;
- docket side covenants as one coordinated settlement; and
- force the king's alternatives to stand beside the exact undertaking they would replace.

Use the Masque to make two or three decisive bargains legible to the entire court; it need not carry every negotiation.

## The order of the evening

### The Procession of Seasons

Each banner enters through its seasonal garden and names the public ground on which it is prepared to act. Eiral and the Ashen Bough enter last because neither satisfies seasonal balance. The procession makes a missing season impossible to hide behind a high seal count.

A house may change its stated ground from the opening audience, but the Master of Mirrors asks whether the earlier statement was false. The truthful answer is almost always no. The court then hears that the house has changed its policy, not discovered a new fact.

Ask a house to name one condition sufficient for a declaration. It may refuse. It may not answer with a condition it knows would still be insufficient.

### The Floor of Satisfaction

Any recognized participant may ask another to acknowledge a public act, accept a correction, or state that an old grievance will not govern the petition. The challenged party may answer, decline, or demand reciprocal language.

This is the natural place to settle Vaudren and Maelith. Several settlements are available.

- Othalan acknowledges that Vaudren's office was omitted from the equinox procession and that the omission diminished its public precedence. He need not confess malicious intent.
- Vaudren accepts a neutral ruling that precedence remains unresolved and agrees not to treat Maelith sponsorship as authorship.
- Both houses appoint champions to a formal contest whose result determines ceremonial order but not political merit.
- The petitioners create a neutral public office for Vaudren within the undertaking, such as Keeper of the Returning Dawn, and Maelith states that the office is not subordinate to its surety role.

A private apology offered elsewhere does not satisfy Vaudren unless the public record changes. A public formula that says nothing meaningful does not survive direct questions beneath the mirrors.

### The Tables of Subscription

Five long tables receive associated instruments: recognition, surety, command, finance, and border defense. A covenant placed on a table is read aloud in summary. Its complete text remains available for inspection. Houses may subscribe, guarantee, witness, or merely acknowledge receipt.

This procedure can create a coordinated package without forcing every bargain into the central petition.

- Ilyrion's Equal Dawn compact can recognize Orison as a treaty partner.
- Maelith can accept named personal guarantors or a reciprocal bond instead of detention.
- Orelle can divide liability among several banners with capped shares.
- Serathiel and Serevin can allocate expedition command, eastern command, reserves, and ward funding.
- Vaudren can receive neutral credit without making the rescue its private triumph.

The Chamberlain warns that public association does not cure contradiction. A side covenant promising mortal authority cannot coexist with a petition granting exclusive royal discretion over every use of the Sunseed. The Masque can expose such conflicts; only the Petition Chamber can resolve them.

### The Declaration of Common Purpose

A coalition approaching seven seals may state one undertaking before the assembled court. The declaration should be broad enough to include the coalition and narrow enough that its members mean the same event.

Examples include:

- restore natural day to Orison while preserving Aurelune's defensibility;
- destroy the Pall without placing Orison under foreign civil rule;
- conduct a joint emergency custody of the Sunseed and return it upon restoration of the sky; or
- preserve both realms against a permanent Shadowfell expansion.

Theron Eiral asks each participating house whether the declaration describes the undertaking it intends to support. A house may answer yes while preserving a separate reason. A qualification enters the public coalition whether invited or not.

Eiral does not require affection. It requires a statement under which later disputes can be adjudicated without pretending the houses joined different ventures.

## The king's open alternatives

Caelir ordered a six-day Crown expedition studied on the first morning. By the Masque, the coalition's public work has supplied what his officers lacked: a passage schedule, a command scheme, a priced border replacement, and a return protocol. He cannot appropriate private promises, but he can assemble public plans into a lawful rival instrument. He offers four alternatives before the oath-mirrors.

### Evacuation without the Sunseed

Royal gates, healers, and roads can remove perhaps one-third of Orison's people. Caelir calls this an immediate plan to save lives. He does not call it a plan to preserve Orison.

This offer appeals to Ilyrion's compassion, Orelle's preference for bounded exposure, and Thalan's resistance to compelled relic custody. Accepting the gates need not end the petition unless the petitioners or a house say that it does.

### A royal expedition

Caelir offers to send the Sunseed under exclusive Crown custody and royal command for six days. The expedition will attempt to break the Pall and will retreat when the term ends or the Dawnward reaches a named threshold.

This can satisfy Serathiel, Maelith, and Serevin while defeating joint custody, Orison's co-authority, and a thirteen-day operational plan. Caelir truthfully describes it as an offer to send the Sunseed. He does not describe it as the undertaking Orison requested.

### Lesser relics

The Crown can provide artifacts sufficient to preserve districts, open evacuation corridors, or prevent the Pall from advancing for a short time. None can restore the sky. Caelir states exactly what each can do.

### Voluntary joinder later

If the coalition becomes broad, protects the Dawnward, and leaves the Crown a meaningful role, Caelir will consider joining an instrument he presently opposes. He does not promise to join. He promises to consider the exact final text rather than refuse it solely because the Concord compelled its drafting.

The king's strategy is not to expose secret divisions. It is to offer each house enough of its public purpose that withdrawing from joint custody can be defended honestly.

## Truthful pressure

The Masque rewards exact questions. Useful questions include:

- "When you say you support saving Orison, do you include preservation of the city and restoration of its sky?"
- "Is this condition sufficient for your declaration, or merely necessary?"
- "Will your declaration remain if the named side covenant is adopted unchanged?"
- "Does your support depend on who receives public credit, or only on the credit article itself?"
- "Which authority in the royal expedition may Orison lawfully refuse?"
- "Do you intend your border pledge to survive if another house commands the expedition?"

A courtier may decline to answer. A refusal beneath an oath-mirror is itself a public political act. Questions delimit commitments the petitioners may later draft; repeated traps merely teach the court to narrow its answers.

## Ways to use the mirrors

### Stage a broad concord

Bring eight or more houses into the Declaration of Common Purpose, adopts neutral credit, and places the security and recognition bargains on separate tables. This strengthens Eiral and makes royal joinder plausible. It also forces the coalition's contradictions into view early.

### Harden a seven-seal bloc

Ask only its intended seven to declare sufficient conditions and defend them publicly. This can produce a disciplined majority. Excluded houses and the king then know exactly which member to peel away.

### Build a reformist public narrative

Center Orison's equality, Aven Tal's claim, and mortal co-custody. The Masque can make those terms politically difficult to strip from the draft. Maelith, Thalan, and the Crown will insist that emergency recognition not silently become general constitutional law.

### Build a security compact

Publicly funds wards, deploys reserves, defines command, and accepts objective recall. Serathiel, Serevin, Orelle, and Thalan become easier to hold. Ilyrion and Orison may find themselves joining an undertaking whose military structure was settled without them.

### Preserve deliberate ambiguity

Decline a common declaration and keep several bargains private until drafting. This prevents premature rupture and forfeits the Masque's strongest protection against later reinterpretation.

## What may remain at dawn

### Conditions become public property

The coalition leaves with a witnessed common purpose, two or more adopted associated instruments, a clear seasonal count, and at least seven houses that have publicly named sufficient conditions for support. The king's alternatives remain available but no longer appear to satisfy the same undertaking.

### A declaration too expensive to soften

- Vaudren receives satisfaction in a form Maelith treats as a lasting loss of precedence.
- Maelith accepts a personal bond only after several party members or allied rulers become answerable guarantors.
- Orelle's consortium spreads liability across houses that demand later influence over the expedition.
- Serevin declares on the strength of deployments that constrain Serathiel's preferred command.
- Eiral accepts the common purpose only after partisan language and sole authorship are removed.
- The petitioners accept royal evacuation while continuing the petition; lives are saved, and Caelir gains public credit for the only aid already underway.

### The king supplies the only coherent story

Treat declarations as disguised seals and accuse withdrawing houses of breaking the oath. The Master of Mirrors states that no false assertion has occurred. Several houses narrow their language, the king's alternatives become the clearest public plan, and the coalition enters drafting with fewer reliable commitments than it had in private.

## What the mirrors keep

- each house's exact declared ground and sufficient conditions;
- the seasonal composition visible in the procession;
- every associated instrument adopted, subscribed, or merely acknowledged;
- the public settlement, if any, between Vaudren and Maelith;
- whether the coalition stated a common purpose and which qualifications entered it;
- which royal alternatives particular houses described as acceptable; and
- any public promise of troops, funds, wards, personal surety, or mortal authority.

## Returning before dawn

The oath-mirrors preserve declarations only until dawn, but certified transcripts remain in the Amber Quill Archive. The Masque itself is not repeated. Later public corrections occur beneath the Argent Canopy or during the Crown Conclave, where the earlier words are read beside the correction.

reference_links.context: Tests whether each public declaration truthfully describes the undertaking a house will support.
Oath-mirrors preserve exact declarations and unanswered questions without turning declarations into seals.
Any seated bearer or regent must declare the exact ground and scope under which the Ashen seal remains available.
Files truthful rival alternatives—evacuation, lesser relics, and a Crown-commanded expedition—against the coalition's public grounds.

encounters.title: The Chamber of the Fourfold Petition
encounters.summary: Lines of seasonal light expose where seven banner bargains touch, and each amendment shows which recognitions and seals it breaks.
encounters.opening_view: One word changes above the square table. Three lines of light snap; a seal lifts; two side covenants begin glowing different colors. Spring, Summer, Autumn, and Winter stand around the same open center, each entered by another door. Pelion reaches for the adverse index. Mara points to the severed line between custody and command. "Whose promise," she asks, "did that word just release?"
encounters.content:
## Situation

The Chamber of the Fourfold Petition has four doors and no central entrance. Spring, Summer, Autumn, and Winter enter separately and meet around a square table cut from one pale tree. The center is open. Above it, the petition hangs in lines of light, each defined term connected to every place it governs.

Contradictions shine in different colors. Compatible bargains share a line of seasonal light; incompatible ones break apart before a seal touches the page. The chamber judges neither justice nor prudence. It makes the coalition visible enough that seven houses cannot seal one page while imagining seven different rescues.

Theron Eiral presides as Chamberlain. Pelion Namaris reads precedent. Mara Venn speaks where Orison has secured authority to speak. The Crown sends an advocate even when the king stays away. Houses may bring counsel, but Orison's petitioners control the petition unless they have granted a sponsor co-authorship.

Come early for model clauses, return with successive drafts, or arrive on the sixth day carrying nearly finished terms. A seal becomes meaningful only when the text identifies the undertaking, custody, command, term, liability, recall, and return—and when each banner can see which promise it will lose if one of those articles changes.

## Three pages around one living text

The chamber keeps three related but distinct dockets.

### The Crown instrument

This is the petition the banners seal and the Chamberlain certifies. It must contain a complete legal undertaking. It cannot delegate its essential meaning to an unpublished promise.

### Associated instruments

Recognition, personal surety, finance, credit, deployment, audit, and border covenants may sit beside the petition. The chamber indexes them and tests them for contradiction. A side covenant may give a house a reason to seal. It may not secretly reverse the central instrument.

### The declaration record

The chamber receives transcripts from the Argent Canopy, the Ashen Bough Hearing, and the Masque. Declarations do not count as seals. They show what a house previously said would be sufficient and make changes of position legible.

Keep a bargain private. It then cannot rely on the chamber to reconcile that bargain with the rest of the coalition.

## How recognitions gather on one text

### 1. State the undertaking

The first article must name what the Sunseed is being used to accomplish.

- **Destroy the Pall** is operationally direct but may permit methods that damage Orison.
- **Preserve Orison** protects the city but leaves disagreement about whether evacuation counts as preservation.
- **Restore natural day to Orison** identifies the desired condition and may require continued custody after the Pall first breaks.
- **Prevent permanent Shadowfell dominion over Orison** is broad enough to justify military action and broad enough to invite it.

Mara Venn can insist that the undertaking not be changed without Orison's consent. Serathiel can insist that ordinary operational decisions remain under command. Both can be true if redirection is distinguished from execution.

### 2. Allocate custody and command

Custody answers who physically holds and legally controls the Sunseed. Command answers who directs people and operations. The court habitually treats them as though one implies the other.

Usable arrangements include:

- joint physical custody by a royal custodian and a mortal co-custodian;
- party command subject to a royal veto limited to damage, prohibited uses, or redirection;
- Serathiel expedition command with Orison retaining civil authority and consent to a changed undertaking;
- rotating custody at named stages; or
- Crown ownership and protective authority without exclusive possession.

A clause giving Caelir "all authority necessary to preserve the Sunseed" is not narrow merely because preservation is a narrow noun. Namaris asks who decides what is necessary.

### 3. Fix the term and return

The petition needs an outside date even if it also ends on completion.

- **Six days** materially reduces Aurelune's exposure and may be too short to save Orison.
- **Thirteen days** supports the expedition plan and increases Dawnward risk.
- **Completion plus an absolute limit** is usually workable if completion is defined.
- **Return upon royal demand** is a unilateral recall under another name.

Return may mean physical delivery to a named official, replanting beneath the throne, or restoration of the Dawnward. These events do not necessarily occur at the same time. Orelle and Namaris care about valuation between delivery and restoration.

### 4. Assign liability

The chamber distinguishes loss from expenditure and fault from risk.

Possible structures include:

- capped shares among participating banners;
- allied guarantees held in trust;
- insurance funded by Orelle and repaid from a defined source;
- liability for proven misuse but not ordinary Dawnward risk;
- Crown assumption of specified background risk; or
- Orison reconstruction revenue without permanent trade privilege.

A promise to make Aurelune whole is not complete until the text identifies which losses count, who values them, and what property is reachable.

### 5. Define defense and recall

The security package may sit partly in deployment covenants, but the petition must state what happens if the Dawnward materially fails.

A strong objective trigger identifies:

- a measurable ward threshold or actual incursion;
- the officials who verify it;
- the response available before full recall;
- who may order recall; and
- whether the undertaking can continue under a shortened route or substitute protection.

Serevin can be given a duty to report and local command without a unilateral power to end the expedition. Serathiel can be given reserves without command over the eastern marches. The text should not solve a command rivalry by granting both officers final authority over the same act.

### 6. State status, credit, and precedent

These clauses determine the political order created by the rescue.

- Orison may be named a treaty partner, protected ally, ward, or participant only for this undertaking.
- Credit may belong to the Crown, the court, the participating banners, Orison's petitioners, or no sole author.
- The instrument may be relic-specific, emergency-only, expressly nonprecedential, or subject to later constitutional review.

A nonprecedential clause limits citation while the event remains in the record. A neutral credit clause leaves boasting untouched while denying sole authorship in the Crown instrument.

## Where the banner bargains touch

Track the draft as linked choices, not a single quality score.

| Article | Broad or reformist form | Narrow or security form | Common fault line |
|---|---|---|---|
| Undertaking | Restore natural day and preserve Orison | Break the Pall or evacuate threatened districts | Whether success means a saved city or saved inhabitants |
| Custody | Royal and mortal co-custodians | Exclusive royal custody or royal protective veto | Whether title is being confused with possession |
| Command | Party or joint expedition command | Eladrin supreme command | Whether command reaches Orison's civil government |
| Term | Completion with a thirteen-day cap | Six-day absolute term | Whether the artifact returns before the work is usable |
| Recall | Multi-party objective trigger | Crown or Serevin unilateral recall | Whether Aurelune can respond without making rescue revocable at will |
| Liability | Shared capped guarantees | Orison collateral or trade privilege | Who pays for risk imposed by saving another realm |
| Return | Delivery plus verified replanting | Delivery to any royal officer | Who bears risk during restoration |
| Credit | Court concord or no sole author | Royal gift or named house leadership | Whether public honor holds or breaks the coalition |
| Precedent | Emergency recognition with later review | Relic-specific sunset and no general citation | Whether the crisis changes constitutional law |
| Orison status | Treaty partner and co-authority | Protected ally or unspecified beneficiary | Whether safeguards become domination |

The columns are neither factions nor ready-made drafts. Cross the table wherever the resulting powers remain jointly obeyable.

## Seals and amendments

A banner seal applies to one exact text. The chamber records why the house says the text is acceptable, but the legal force attaches to the words rather than the explanation.

Amendments fall into three practical classes.

### Corrections without changed effect

Spelling, numbering, cross-references, and a definition made explicit without changing its scope may be certified as corrections. The Chamberlain reads the correction aloud. Any banner may demand reaffirmation, but the correction does not automatically release seals.

### Material amendments to one article

A changed command power, term, liability share, recall trigger, status clause, or associated instrument releases every seal whose stated condition depends on that change. Other banners remain sealed unless they reserved broader conditions. The chamber asks each house to state that dependence on the record.

### A changed undertaking

Changing the named purpose or replacing joint custody with an exclusive scheme releases all seals. That amendment creates a new petition.

A released house may reaffirm immediately. It need not renegotiate from the beginning unless the amendment actually defeats its settlement. Public declarations and prior bargaining make reaffirmation easier, not automatic.

A seal cast by a temporary or scope-limited banner-holder is also bounded by the order that created the office. A correction within the authorized undertaking may be reaffirmed normally. A changed undertaking, a use outside the authorized covenants, or a term extending beyond the office requires renewed authority before that seal can attach to the revised text.

## What the Chamberlain can recognize

Theron examines the petition in his official capacity. Certification requires:

- seven seals on the same exact text;
- at least one Spring, Summer, Autumn, and Winter seal;
- a named undertaking and outside term;
- internally coherent custody, command, recall, liability, and return;
- a preserved royal interest; and
- associated instruments that do not contradict the petition.

Theron must identify a defect specifically. He cannot say only that the text is unwise or politically dangerous. He may require correction, schedule a correction session, and refuse to certify language whose validity depends on an aggressive interpretation.

House Eiral may withhold its banner while the Chamberlain certifies. It may seal while Theron warns that another clause is defective. The roles do not merge because the same person performs them.

## The Crown draft

The royal advocate files Caelir's alternative once the coalition's working draft becomes credible. It offers a six-day royal expedition under exclusive Crown custody, a defined evacuation program, lesser relics for protected districts, and full Crown liability for royal acts. Orison receives consultation but no authority to redirect or refuse royal use within the expedition.

The Crown draft leaves the petition valid and gives wavering houses a complete alternative consistent with their public purposes. Borrow its security clauses, negotiate toward voluntary joinder, or reject it and hold seven seals.

## Shapes one coalition may truthfully inhabit

### Draft a narrow Crown instrument with broad side covenants

The petition carries only the undertaking, custody, command, term, recall, liability, and return. Recognition, surety, credit, finance, and deployments sit in associated instruments. This limits precedent and makes contradictions easier to isolate. It depends on houses trusting covenants outside the central text.

### Draft one broad political compact

The petition itself names Orison's equality, neutral credit, shared defense, and constitutional limits. The victory becomes difficult to disaggregate later. Every amendment threatens more seals.

### Build staged custody

The Sunseed begins under joint custody, passes to expedition custody on departure, and returns to royal custody after the Pall breaks or the term expires. Staging can reconcile several houses and creates dangerous transition points if poorly defined.

### Seek royal joinder

Adopt enough Crown protections that Caelir can join voluntarily without obtaining exclusive command. This helps Eiral and Thalan and may cost reformist credit or operational freedom.

### Hold a bare majority

Refuse late improvements that would release one of its seven seals. The resulting instrument may be inelegant but valid. The king will test every seam at the Conclave.

## How the sitting may close

### Seven houses seal the same undertaking

The coalition leaves with a complete exact petition, at least seven seals including all four seasons, associated instruments indexed without contradiction, and a correction plan for any narrow defect. Each sealed house can state why the actual text satisfies it.

### A sound text that sheds support

- Orison receives real authority only through a side covenant whose guarantors now own part of the political victory.
- The security package holds Winter and Summer at the price of a shortened term or a restrictive recall article.
- Liability is bounded by granting Orelle influence over valuation and post-rescue repayment.
- Thalan's sunset protects the Crown and narrows the reformers' precedent.
- Vaudren's credit clause keeps Summer balance but makes royal joinder less likely.
- A late amendment releases one or more seals and consumes the time reserved for final lobbying.

### The page proves the coalition never agreed

Ask the chamber to preserve ambiguous language because different houses understood it differently. Namaris identifies the conflicting effects, Theron refuses certification, and the chamber records that the coalition has not yet agreed on one undertaking. The petition remains amendable; the court day is lost and the Crown draft becomes the only complete instrument on file.

## What enters the certified record

- the exact Crown instrument and every associated instrument;
- which banners are sealed, released, declared, open, or opposed;
- the stated dependency of each seal on particular articles;
- every correction the Chamberlain has required;
- the final seasonal composition;
- whether Caelir has been invited to join and on what terms;
- whether Orison's representative has accepted the undertaking; and
- how much time remains for reaffirmation before the Conclave.

## On a return

The chamber remains open until the Conclave. A late correction is possible; a late redesign is a new petition. Let the political cost follow the houses whose bargains change.
