encounters.content:
## Situation

On Court Day Seven the Argent Canopy descends until its silver leaves form a circle around the throne. The glass root opens. The Sunseed rises into view: a fruit no larger than a clenched hand, bright enough to throw four shadows, one toward each season.

The banner standards stand around it. If the Ashen Bough remains vacant, its empty place is not removed. If Eiral has withheld its seal, the Twilight Laurel still faces the throne. The court has spent six days speaking about custody. Now the thing to be carried is close enough to warm every hand in the room.

No argument arrives as a surprise. The Sunseed does not count seals; it throws the coalition's named powers into four seasonal shadows and exposes where two banners still imagine different custodians, commands, or returns. The Conclave tests which declarations, covenants, and compromises survive proximity to the relic and the king's complete alternative. A banner may reaffirm, withdraw, or join the Crown. Its explanation must be true; generosity, completeness, and courage remain optional.

## How the Sunseed reads the coalition

### 1. The seasonal call

Theron calls Spring, Summer, Autumn, and Winter before he counts seals. Eiral and the Ashen Bough are called afterward. The order makes seasonal balance visible before the count.

An eighth unseasoned seal cannot cure a missing season. Bargaining remains open until the final call.

### 2. The petition is read

Pelion Namaris reads the exact Crown instrument and identifies every associated instrument by title and parties. He does not summarize away difficult clauses. Any house may ask that a definition or linked covenant be read in full.

Mara Venn or another authorized representative of Orison states whether the named undertaking is accepted. Orison's acceptance is not a legal substitute for seven banners. It demonstrates that the coalition has not secured the Sunseed for an undertaking the city itself rejects.

### 3. Certification or defect

Theron either certifies the petition or identifies each defect. His reasons are reviewable against the Concord. Political objections do not become defects merely because the Chamberlain shares them.

A narrow contradiction, failed cross-reference, or omitted verifier may be corrected in recess. Banners affected by the correction reaffirm. A changed undertaking, exclusive-custody substitution, or new liability scheme requires a new instrument and releases the existing seals.

Caelir may argue that a clause is dangerous, unprecedented, or dishonorable. He may not command the Chamberlain to misstate its validity.

### 4. The declaration record

The Master of Mirrors reads each relevant declaration beside the house's present posture. A house may withdraw. It must then say which condition failed, which fact changed, or which public purpose it now ranks above the earlier one.

The Conclave turns inconsistency into authorship. A banner may leave the coalition under its own name.

### 5. The royal instrument of relief

Caelir presents a complete alternative.

- The Sunseed travels for six days under exclusive Crown custody and royal command.
- Orison's representatives are consulted and may refuse civil cooperation, but they have no authority over the relic.
- The Crown assumes liability for royal misuse and funds immediate evacuation corridors.
- Lesser relics protect selected districts if the Pall cannot be broken within the term.
- The Sunseed returns automatically upon the term's end or a defined Dawnward failure.
- The Crown claims the undertaking as royal relief rather than compelled joint custody.

Caelir states that this instrument saves every life and district his officers can reach without surrendering the trust placed in the Crown. He does not claim that it is as likely to restore Orison's sky as the longer joint-custody plan. He does not claim that Orison governs its own rescue.

Houses may support the royal instrument and withdraw from the petition without speaking falsely. The king's strongest argument is that their declared purposes can be served without the constitutional and military risks of the coalition's text.

### 6. Final questions

Each banner may ask one question of Orison's petitioners, one of the Crown, and one of another house. Refusal is an answer. Keep the questions on text and declared commitment, not concealed motive.

Useful final questions include:

- "Which act by the royal custodian is beyond the purpose-limited veto?"
- "What happens on the seventh day if the Pall is broken but natural day has not returned?"
- "Which guarantor pays first if the eastern ward fails without an invasion?"
- "May Orison refuse a use of the Sunseed against its civil authorities?"
- "Will House Eiral seal if the Crown does not join?"
- "Will this house preserve its deployment after another house receives public credit?"
- "Does the Ashen Bough's authority extend through the entire custody term?"

Answer by pointing to the instrument. An answer that depends on an unwritten assurance is an invitation to amend or withdraw.

### 7. The seals are called

Each banner is called once. It may seal, reaffirm, withdraw, or abstain. A conditional seal is not a seal. A house may first demand that an already permitted correction be made; it may not rewrite the undertaking during its vote and pretend the other seals remain attached.

When seven valid seals including all four seasons stand on the same certified text, the Concord binds the Crown. Caelir's personal assent is unnecessary.

If eight or more banners seal, the court treats the petition as a broad act even if the king remains opposed. If Caelir joins voluntarily, he does so after certification and before transfer. His joinder strengthens the political settlement; it is not the source of its validity.

## Holding the pattern of banners together

Use only the pressure that fits the coalition actually assembled.

### Reformist coalition

Ilyrion and an Aven-led Ashen Bough emphasize Orison's equality. Caelir offers evacuation and royal relief that save lives while removing mortal co-authority. Thalan and Maelith ask whether emergency recognition has become a general inheritance and sovereignty rule.

The coalition holds if recognition is real, the relic petition remains bounded, and personal surety does not become wardship by another name.

### Martial coalition

Serathiel, Serevin, and a Mirath-led Ashen Bough emphasize command and defense. Caelir's exclusive expedition appears close to their stated objectives. Ilyrion or Vaudren may refuse to ratify a rescue that becomes solely a Crown military act.

The coalition holds if command is coherent, Orison retains civil authority and consent to redirection, and the border package survives without unrestricted recall.

### Mercantile coalition

Orelle and Namaris anchor liability, audit, and return. The king offers Crown-funded relief with lower exposure. Reformers ask whether Orison is being saved into debt; military houses ask whether valuation procedures will delay action.

The coalition holds if liability is bounded, funding is executable, and repayment does not purchase domination.

### Constitutional coalition

Thalan, Namaris, and Eiral emphasize narrow precedent, exact process, and royal dignity. Caelir invites them to accept voluntary royal relief and avoid compulsion entirely. Other houses may suspect that the undertaking has been narrowed until it cannot save the city.

The coalition holds if the emergency finding is genuine, the operational term remains usable, and restraint does not become disguised refusal.

### Bare majority

With exactly seven seals, every withdrawal is decisive. The king addresses each house separately and offers it a true route to part of its public purpose. The petitioners cannot answer by claiming the houses are secretly bribed or lying. They must show why the joint undertaking better satisfies the grounds they chose to make public.

### Broad concord

With eight or more seals, the king attacks the text rather than peeling one house: too many owners, authorities, and promises. A broad coalition must show a real conflict-resolution structure and common purpose. It is the coalition most likely to receive voluntary royal joinder.

## Royal conduct on defeat

Caelir honors a valid Concord. He meant to win.

If compelled, he says:

> The court has placed its hands upon a trust that was mine to guard. I will not call lawful hands thieves. I will require them to carry what they have taken responsibility for.

He then performs every duty the instrument assigns him. He interprets every ambiguity in favor of the Crown and Aurelune. A clean petition produces stern cooperation. A humiliating petition produces exact obedience without generosity.

If persuaded or reconciled, Caelir joins after certification and names the undertaking a concord between Crown, banners, and Orison. The conflict remains in the record.

## Outcomes

### Broad concord

At least eight banners seal, the security package is credible, Orison holds meaningful authority, the text preserves a real Crown interest, and no single bloc owns the rescue. Caelir may join voluntarily. The Sunseed leaves with the best chance of preserving both realms, though many houses acquire durable claims on the settlement.

### Royal concord

Seven or more seasonally balanced banners certify a petition strong enough to compel the Crown, then Caelir joins after negotiating real changes to command, term, credit, custody, or royal dignity. His joinder improves cooperation and lets the undertaking be presented as reconciliation rather than defeat. The seals remain the source of the coalition's leverage, and the negotiated concessions remain binding costs rather than ceremonial language.

### Compelled loan

Seven banners and all four seasons seal a valid petition over Caelir's opposition. The Sunseed leaves. Every burden in the text travels with it: command limits, guarantors, recall triggers, liability, public credit, and the outside date.

### Partisan victory

A reformist, martial, mercantile, dynastic, or constitutional bloc supplies the decisive structure. The petition succeeds and the rescue becomes evidence for that bloc's program. Other houses comply while preparing the next contest.

### Constitutional rupture

The text is valid, but the coalition humiliates the Crown, seats a contested claimant solely to manufacture a vote, or forces certification through the most aggressive lawful reading. The Sunseed leaves under law. The court fractures around who will bear the precedent.

### Royal relief

The petition loses support or the petitioners choose the Crown instrument. The Sunseed may still travel under exclusive royal control, or evacuation and lesser relics may save many lives. Orison's sky is less likely to be restored, and the Crown defines the undertaking.

### Failure with consequence

No valid instrument survives before departure becomes impossible. The court still implements any evacuation, border, recognition, succession, or alliance agreements the petitioners secured. Orison suffers the Pall, but political play has changed Aurelune rather than resetting it.

## Transfer of the Sunseed

On a successful petition, the glass root divides according to the custody article. A royal custodian takes one handle of the root-casket. Each other named custodian receives the authority and physical access stated in the text. If the petition created only nominal joint custody, the ceremony makes that failure visible immediately.

Theron reads the undertaking, term, recall trigger, and act of return. Each custodian answers with the exact promise the oath will enforce. Trust is not among the required answers.

The root-casket enters the Crown Passage before moonrise. The passage reaches Orison's western gate; from there, one road still remembers the way to the Pall's center. The custody term begins when the Sunseed leaves the throne root, not when the court week began. A late correction, six-day term, recall threshold, command compromise, or unfinished deployment is now an operational fact rather than court rhetoric.

## What leaves the throne hall

- the final certified petition and associated instruments;
- the banners that sealed, withdrew, or joined the Crown instrument;
- whether Caelir was compelled, reconciled, or voluntarily joined;
- the Sunseed's named custodians and command structure;
- the outside date and exact recall trigger;
- the active border, liability, surety, recognition, and credit obligations;
- the Ashen Bough settlement and its duration; and
- the public account of who saved Orison, protected Aurelune, or accepted the cost of failure.

## If the court is reconvened

The Conclave ends the court campaign; its consequences remain. Later play may bring the adventurers back to answer for loss, delayed return, a recalled relic, an inheritance precedent, unpaid guarantees, or a rescue that succeeded under politically intolerable terms.

revelations.title: House Ilyrion can seal for sovereign partnership
revelations.description: Ilyrion can support when Orison is treated as a treaty partner, a mortal shares meaningful authority, and the undertaking cannot be redirected without defined mortal consent. Recognition may sit in the petition or in a guaranteed side compact.

revelations.title: House Maelith can seal for answerable personal surety
revelations.description: Maelith can support through narrow fosterage, reciprocal hostages, named banner guarantors, an enforceable personal bond, or a royal co-custodian. The form must answer for custody and return without silently making Orison a dependent.

revelations.title: House Serathiel can seal for coherent command and defense
revelations.description: Serathiel can support when the expedition has a workable command structure and Aurelune receives a reserve, substitute ward, allied deployment, or other credible protection during the loan.

revelations.title: House Vaudren can seal after public satisfaction or neutral credit
revelations.description: Vaudren can support through a meaningful Maelith acknowledgment, a limited precedence ruling, neutral authorship, or a real public office that gives the house independent honor in the undertaking.

revelations.title: House Orelle can seal for bounded and assigned liability
revelations.description: Orelle can support when the material risk to Aurelune is valued and assigned through collateral, shared guarantees, limited trade rights, insurance, or a term and ward package that makes losses bearable.

revelations.title: House Namaris can seal for exact and reviewable language
revelations.description: Namaris can support a petition with defined custody, return, audit, and precedent effects. It accepts narrow drafting, a sunset and review, or side covenants that keep house-specific bargains out of the central instrument.

revelations.title: House Thalan can seal for restrained emergency precedent
revelations.description: Thalan can support through a finding of necessity, a short or bounded term, preserved royal co-custody, a sunset, or voluntary royal joinder. It will not support a text designed to celebrate the Crown’s defeat.

revelations.title: House Serevin can seal for a defended eastern border
revelations.description: Serevin can support through replacement troops, substitute wards, Serathiel reserves, a shorter term, or a carefully defined recall mechanism responsive to an objective breach rather than ordinary seasonal movement.

revelations.title: House Eiral can seal for a governable concord
revelations.description: Eiral can support a broad coalition, seven seals plus royal joinder, or a petition with neutral leadership and explicit conflict resolution. The house resists a bare majority held together only by incompatible private bargains.

revelations.title: The Ashen Bough can be seated before the Conclave
revelations.description: A timely hearing can seat Lady Mirath, seat Aven Tal, establish a temporary regency, or leave the banner vacant by decision rather than neglect. The result changes coalition alignments but supplies no seasonal balance.

revelations.title: Public declarations can bind politically without becoming seals
revelations.description: A witnessed statement beneath the Canopy or at the Masque does not create a legal banner seal, but it gives rivals, dependents, and the court a truthful record that makes abandonment costly.

revelations.title: A complete petition can compel certification
revelations.description: The Chamberlain must certify a valid, internally consistent text. He can require correction, control the schedule of correction, and distinguish his official duty from House Eiral’s political support.

revelations.title: The king’s counteroffer can be defeated without persuading him
revelations.description: Caelir begins evacuation and commissions a six-day Crown expedition at once, then uses the court's public passage, command, finance, and defense work to make that rival plan executable. A stable seven-seal coalition can reject it and compel joint custody even while the king remains opposed.

revelations.title: The Concord can compel joint custody without transferring ownership
revelations.description: The petition may preserve Crown ownership and a meaningful royal interest while granting the party, Orison, or other named custodians enough possession and authority to complete the undertaking.

revelations.title: Seasonal balance is separate from the seven-seal count
revelations.description: A valid petition needs at least one Spring, Summer, Autumn, and Winter banner among its seven seals. Eiral and the Ashen Bough can increase the count but cannot substitute for a missing season.

revelations.title: A combined security package can protect Aurelune during the loan
revelations.description: Temporary wards, allied deployments, eastern reserves, a bounded term, and objective recall procedures can reduce the real danger of removing the Sunseed without giving any single actor an unrestricted power to end the rescue.

revelations.title: Side covenants can carry compatible house bargains
revelations.description: Recognition, surety, credit, financing, audit, and command protocols can be placed in parallel instruments if the central petition still states the complete legal undertaking and the covenants do not contradict it.

revelations.title: Orison’s agency can survive custody and command safeguards
revelations.description: The coalition can name Orison as a sovereign participant, give a mortal co-custodian real authority, and preserve a right to resist redirection while still providing personal surety, military command, and enforceable return terms.

clues.title: Ilyrion’s partner clause
clues.description: Saelira says Ilyrion will seal only if Orison stands inside the undertaking as a party to its own preservation. Rethan Sol reduces the phrase to treaty standing, mortal co-authority, and a right to refuse redirection.
clues.discovery: Heard in Ilyrion’s opening declaration; one direct question forces Saelira to say what power the word “party” must carry.

clues.title: Maelith’s named-person requirement
clues.description: Othalan says a city cannot answer for a relic, but a named person can. Asked whether fosterage is indispensable, he concedes that any enforceable personal surety can satisfy Maelith.
clues.discovery: Heard among the opening positions. The alternatives appear only after someone separates surety from fosterage.

clues.title: Serathiel’s two-part objection
clues.description: Ysandre separates two demands the court is inclined to hear as one: command of the expedition and defense of Aurelune. She will bargain over the first once the coalition names a reserve, substitute ward, or allied deployment for the second.
clues.discovery: Spoken before the whole court and entered in the public minutes.

clues.title: The Red Rose objection to Maelith leadership
clues.description: Avar refuses to place the Rose beneath the Hart. Theron translates the image into three legal exits: satisfaction, equal precedence, or a coalition led by neither house.
clues.discovery: Heard in the opening exchange; Theron supplies the translation when asked what would actually change Vaudren’s position.

clues.title: The Chamberlain’s compulsory duty
clues.description: Theron cannot reject a valid petition or certify an inconsistent one. He must require correction, though his office controls the calendar and order in which correction occurs.
clues.discovery: Read with the Concord of Open Hands.

clues.title: Seven is not the whole count
clues.description: Seven seals are required, and Spring, Summer, Autumn, and Winter must all appear among them. Eiral and a seated Ashen Bough add to the count but cannot replace a missing season.
clues.discovery: Read aloud before the opening audience disperses.

clues.title: Declarations bind reputation, not the seal
clues.description: A witnessed declaration may be withdrawn without oath-breaking. If it was made beneath the Canopy or at the Masque, the withdrawal must enter the same public record under the speaker’s name.
clues.discovery: Heard when Theron distinguishes declarations from seals.

clues.title: The Concord compels custody rather than alienation
clues.description: The Crown may retain title while named custodians receive possession and authority for the undertaking. Caelir’s ownership does not entail exclusive operational control.
clues.discovery: Established by asking which royal interest the Concord must preserve.

clues.title: The Crown expedition needs the same defenses
clues.description: Caelir’s six-day expedition remains a paper order until the court opens the passage, procures substitute warding, fixes command, and places reserves on the eastern marches. Those works answer the danger of removing the Sunseed under either instrument.
clues.discovery: Compare the royal order with Theron’s hearing calendar. Four dependencies are marked unfinished in both dockets.

clues.title: Reciprocal surety without wardship
clues.description: Rethan Sol identifies an old equal-treaty form in which each party entrusts a named protected guest to the other. Maelith can obtain personal answerability without holding a unilateral ward.
clues.discovery: Offered directly when the party asks how Ilyrion would distinguish reciprocal surety from subordination.

clues.title: Ilyrion’s route through Aven Tal
clues.description: Ilyrion will sponsor an accelerated hearing for Aven Tal and treat his sealed adoption as a serious claim. Saelira admits that seating him would also strengthen her preferred recognition coalition.
clues.discovery: Obtained from Saelira without persuasion; she does not conceal the political benefit.

clues.title: People saved, city surrendered
clues.description: Caelir can truthfully call evacuation a plan to save Orison’s people. It preserves neither the city, its institutions, nor most of its population from the Pall.
clues.discovery: Presented in Ilyrion’s public answer to the royal offer.

clues.title: The recognition compact can run beside the petition
clues.description: Rethan drafts a separate Equal Dawn compact that recognizes Orison as a treaty partner without enlarging the relic petition’s constitutional precedent. It requires a credible witness and adoption before Ilyrion seals.
clues.discovery: Produced whenever the party asks to separate political recognition from relic custody.

clues.title: A mortal co-custodian with a defined refusal right
clues.description: Ilyrion proposes that Orison’s representative share custody and may refuse only a redirection of the named undertaking, not ordinary route or safety orders. The distinction preserves agency without creating a general operational veto.
clues.discovery: Heard in the first revised form of the Equal Dawn declaration.

clues.title: A non-exploitative guarantee for Orelle
clues.description: Ilyrion can support a capped guarantee funded by allied states, participating banners, or reconstruction revenue offered on ordinary terms. Orelle receives answerable security without acquiring permanent privilege over Orison.
clues.discovery: Produced when Saelira distinguishes shared responsibility from trade concessions imposed as the price of rescue.

clues.title: Ilyrion asks for a hand, not a title
clues.description: Saelira requires Orison to hold real custody or authority during the undertaking, but none of her acceptable forms transfers ownership of the Sunseed. Equality requires a hand on the trust, not a new title to it.
clues.discovery: Ask whether Orison must own the relic. Saelira cuts the word “owner” from a proposed clause and leaves “co-custodian” untouched.

clues.title: Equal standing through reciprocal hostages
clues.description: Lady Senra offers to enter Orison’s protection if a mortal envoy enters Maelith’s. The reciprocal structure gives Ilyrion a way to accept personal surety as equality rather than wardship.
clues.discovery: Senra makes the offer openly when both houses’ objections are placed side by side.

clues.title: The apology Vaudren could accept
clues.description: The Gallery records distinguish an apology for pain from acknowledgment of a chosen public act. Othalan can satisfy Vaudren by admitting that he chose an order that diminished the house, even if he denies intending every consequence.
clues.discovery: Established by comparing the existing draft apology with the Gallery’s own record of the procession.

clues.title: A bond against named estates
clues.description: Master Halven Roe identifies a precedent in which several noble estates guaranteed the return of a Crown trust. Namaris can adapt the form if default, valuation, and audit are stated exactly.
clues.discovery: Provided when the party asks for security that does not place a mortal under Maelith authority.

clues.title: Maelith’s bounded regency settlement
clues.description: Maelith will support Lady Mirath as a military regent if the office ends after the Sunseed undertaking and leaves the ultimate inheritance unresolved. The banner could then vote under the regency.
clues.discovery: Othalan offers this as a way to secure the Ashen Bough without recognizing Aven’s adoption claim.

clues.title: Fosterage can be kept outside the relic text
clues.description: The house accepts a separate, time-bounded fosterage instrument so long as the central petition identifies the resulting guarantor. This keeps kinship powers from silently becoming conditions of relic custody.
clues.discovery: Explained by Halven when the party asks which promises must appear in the petition itself.

clues.title: The powers inside a gracious noun
clues.description: The Gallery plaques distinguish protected person, fosterling, ward, and hostage. A gracious noun may still carry powers over residence, marriage, departure, or succession unless the instrument removes them.
clues.discovery: Visible in Maelith’s standard forms and confirmed by asking what each relation permits the house to do.

clues.title: Maelith binds the bearer rather than the owner
clues.description: Othalan’s surety forms attach answerability to the person, office, or estate carrying custody and return duties. Crown title can remain intact while someone other than the Crown becomes legally answerable for the relic’s use and return.
clues.discovery: Compare the royal co-custody form with the banner-surety plaques. The owner’s name stays fixed while the answering name changes.

clues.title: The priced reserve package
clues.description: Serathiel has costed three replacement-defense plans. Orelle can finance the least expensive through shared banner guarantees rather than a permanent claim on Orison’s customs.
clues.discovery: The figures lie on the public war table; the financing structure appears when the party asks who could underwrite them.

clues.title: Border command is distinct from expedition command
clues.description: Ysandre concedes that Serevin can command the eastern reserve while another actor commands the expedition. The distinction can satisfy both houses if recall authority is separately defined.
clues.discovery: Elicited by asking whether Serathiel’s command demand extends to troops that remain in Aurelune.

clues.title: A divided command that can still move
clues.description: Corven’s divided scheme assigns custody, guard, expedition command, and civil consent to different actors, with Eiral chairing a narrow conflict panel. It works only if silence cannot serve as a veto.
clues.discovery: Found among the plans Corven produces after the party asks to see every prepared option.

clues.title: The exclusive-command counter-petition
clues.description: Serathiel expects Caelir to offer the Sunseed under exclusive royal command once a majority appears possible. The offer can peel away houses that care more about use of the relic than joint custody.
clues.discovery: Ysandre states this prediction openly because she considers it the prudent royal answer.

clues.title: The combined Dawnward replacement
clues.description: Temporary wardstones, two allied companies, and a Serevin-controlled mobile reserve can replace most of the Sunseed’s border function for thirteen days. No single component is sufficient alone.
clues.discovery: Displayed as one of the full alternatives at the war table.

clues.title: The war table separates redirection from field command
clues.description: Corven’s divided-command schemes let Orison refuse a changed undertaking or a use against its civil government while leaving route, timing, and safety orders to the expedition commander. Agency need not become a veto over ordinary movement.
clues.discovery: Run the same crisis twice, once as a route change and once as a change of purpose. The command markers pass to different hands.

clues.title: The campaign order can stand beside the petition
clues.description: The expedition’s chain of command, reserve deployments, and crisis procedure can live in a linked campaign order, provided the central petition names the controlling powers and the order cannot contradict custody, purpose, or recall.
clues.discovery: Corven produces a campaign-order cover sheet already indexed to the draft Crown instrument rather than written into it.

clues.title: The acknowledgment beneath witnesses
clues.description: Vaudren will accept Maelith’s continued participation if Othalan acknowledges that he chose the disputed order and accepts equal precedence for the Sunseed undertaking. Maelith need not confess malicious intent.
clues.discovery: Avar states the minimum formula when asked what satisfaction would end rather than merely suspend the grievance.

clues.title: The two kinds of precedence
clues.description: Ivara’s records and Namaris precedent distinguish genealogical order from ceremonial order. A ruling limited to the present undertaking can be exact without rewriting every future procession.
clues.discovery: Obtained from the Pavilion’s record table and confirmed by requesting an archival determination.

clues.title: The court may own the rescue collectively
clues.description: Vaudren will join a petition presented under the Twilight Laurel or simply under the ten banners if Maelith also renounces senior authorship. Eiral values the same formula because it preserves royal dignity and coalition breadth.
clues.discovery: Avar offers neutral authorship as an alternative to apology.

clues.title: The Masque can convert satisfaction into commitment
clues.description: A Maelith acknowledgment and Vaudren acceptance made beneath the portable oath-mirrors become a public record neither house can later redescribe without cost, even before either seal is affixed.
clues.discovery: Ivara recommends the Masque when the party asks for a settlement stronger than privacy but earlier than the petition.

clues.title: The Crown can purchase Vaudren with visible honor
clues.description: Caelir can offer Vaudren command of the evacuation gates, first place in the relief procession, and public credit without lending the Sunseed. The offer satisfies honor while defeating the party’s undertaking.
clues.discovery: Avar admits the offer would be serious when asked what the king could give her besides the relic.

clues.title: Credit can be fixed outside custody law
clues.description: A witnessed protocol can assign speaking order, public credit, and ceremonial precedence without loading those matters into the relic petition. Vaudren accepts if the protocol is adopted before the Conclave.
clues.discovery: Drafted by Ivara once the party separates public authorship from legal custody.

clues.title: A guarantee Ilyrion can defend
clues.description: Orelle can accept guarantees from allied cities, participating banners, or court revenue instead of permanent Orison trade privileges. The rescue then assigns cost without converting emergency dependence into subordination.
clues.discovery: Produced when the party compares Orison trade privileges with allied guarantors and shared ward bonds.

clues.title: The reserve can be financed without expedition command
clues.description: Orelle can fund replacement troops and wardstones while Serathiel yields personal command of the expedition. The military objection becomes a priced public obligation rather than a demand for control.
clues.discovery: Produced when Orelle prices an eastern reserve separately from expedition command.

clues.title: Only unrecoverable losses need indemnity
clues.description: Namaris can define compensable loss to exclude investments that remain Orelle property and ordinary expenses Aurelune would bear anyway. The narrower schedule is auditable and still protects real damage.
clues.discovery: Obtained by classifying each schedule entry as loss, capital, advantage, or reserve.

clues.title: Border ward bonds
clues.description: Orelle can issue short-term bonds funding Serevin’s wardstones and reserve. Repayment can be shared among banners rather than charged solely to Orison.
clues.discovery: Available among the Exchange’s short-term instruments once the ward package has named performance and duration.

clues.title: Joint custody is cheaper than transferred ownership
clues.description: Orelle’s risk tables treat Crown ownership with bounded joint custody as materially safer than a transfer. The legal distinction reduces the required collateral without depriving the party of operational possession.
clues.discovery: Visible in the separate valuation columns for Crown title, operational custody, and outright transfer.

clues.title: The complete security package has a price
clues.description: Orelle can finance temporary wards, transport, and an eastern reserve for thirteen days if liability is shared and procurement begins before the fourth court day.
clues.discovery: Presented when the party asks for the complete thirteen-day Dawnward package and authorizes procurement before the fourth court day.

clues.title: The royal alternative transfers rather than removes cost
clues.description: Orelle’s ledgers show that evacuation leaves abandoned property, displaced citizens, and the lost city on Orison’s account. Caelir’s plan is cheaper to Aurelune because it transfers loss, not because it preserves more.
clues.discovery: Established by asking Mirelle to price the royal evacuation plan under the same categories as the Sunseed undertaking.

clues.title: Orelle prices each associated promise separately
clues.description: The Exchange keeps financing, guarantees, procurement, and political compensation in separate ledgers linked to the petition. The separation exposes who pays without turning every debt or trade concession into a condition of custody.
clues.discovery: Follow one red thread across the account wall. It crosses four signed schedules and enters the Crown instrument only at the liability article.

clues.title: A liability share does not buy command
clues.description: Orelle’s tables distinguish payer, guarantor, custodian, and commander. Orison may accept a bounded share of loss or repayment without granting the creditor authority over its civil government, the expedition’s purpose, or the Sunseed.
clues.discovery: Ask Mirelle which column grants orders. She taps four headings and says none of them does unless another instrument says so.

clues.title: The personal-bond precedent
clues.description: A prior relic loan was secured by three named estates rather than a ward or hostage. The form gives Maelith personal answerability while preserving the beneficiary’s sovereign status.
clues.discovery: Identified in the Three Estates Bond and converted into a present surety clause at the drafting table.

clues.title: A limited ceremonial ruling
clues.description: Namaris precedent permits the court to determine precedence for one undertaking without deciding the general rank of the houses. Vaudren can receive public satisfaction without making Maelith legally junior forever.
clues.discovery: Heard in the procession precedents when the party asks to decide rank for one undertaking rather than for all purposes.

clues.title: The narrow necessity finding
clues.description: The oldest Concord cases distinguish existential necessity from ordinary foreign aid. A recital tied to the Pall’s permanent effects and the Shadowfell’s expansion can place Orison within the narrow standard.
clues.discovery: Produced by reading the Briar Compulsion together with its later limiting judgments through an adverse index.

clues.title: Certification and support are separate acts
clues.description: The Chamberlain must certify a valid text even if House Eiral withholds its banner. Conversely, Eiral may seal and still require official correction of a defect.
clues.discovery: Read in the office precedents for chamberlains who also bear a Great Banner.

clues.title: A defective petition may be corrected without restarting
clues.description: If amendments preserve the named undertaking and every affected banner reaffirms, the Chamberlain can certify a corrected text without a new petition cycle. Unaffected seals need not be repeated.
clues.discovery: Heard in the amendment rules once the party distinguishes material terms from clerical correction.

clues.title: Parallel instruments are lawful but subordinate
clues.description: Side covenants may govern recognition, surety, financing, credit, audit, and command detail. They cannot contradict custody, term, recall, or return in the central petition.
clues.discovery: Read directly from the Archive’s rule on associated instruments and tested against the proposed covenant set.

clues.title: Recognition can be operative without becoming general doctrine
clues.description: Namaris can name Orison a treaty partner for custody, command consultation, and consent to redirection while expressly reserving broader constitutional questions. Ilyrion gains real equality inside the undertaking without forcing Thalan to accept a universal rule.
clues.discovery: Produced when the party asks for the narrowest clause that still gives Orison enforceable political standing.

clues.title: A mortal custodian can block redirection without blocking tactics
clues.description: The petition can require mortal consent for any change of undertaking, destination, or use against Orison’s civil authorities while leaving ordinary operational decisions to the agreed command structure.
clues.discovery: Heard in the Archive’s clause separating strategic redirection from tactical command.

clues.title: The adverse index keeps four hands apart
clues.description: Namaris indexes ownership, custody, possession, and use as separate legal acts. One instrument can leave title with the Crown, place the root-casket in shared hands, and grant operational use to the named undertaking.
clues.discovery: Read the four-column adverse index against Caelir’s opening refusal. Exclusive Crown custody appears as one option, not a consequence of ownership.

clues.title: The certification index tests count and season separately
clues.description: The Archive’s certification rubric has independent lines for seven valid seals and representation of Spring, Summer, Autumn, and Winter. A surplus seal cannot cure a blank seasonal line.
clues.discovery: Pelion turns the rubric sideways. The count column can be complete while the seasonal square remains visibly open.

clues.title: Recognition can be calendared without broadening the emergency rule
clues.description: Thalan will tolerate a separate constitutional compact on Orison’s status if it is calendared after the crisis and sponsored now. Ilyrion can accept the sequence if the later proceeding is not merely aspirational.
clues.discovery: Offered when the party separates emergency action from a scheduled post-crisis recognition convention.

clues.title: Sunset and review satisfy both conservative houses
clues.description: A relic-specific sunset, audit, and formal review give Namaris exact closure and Thalan assurance that the emergency rule will not silently become general law.
clues.discovery: Set out in the narrow-necessity draft placed on the frozen record.

clues.title: Recall may turn on a defined breach
clues.description: Thalan accepts a recall process triggered by measurable Dawnward failure and confirmed by multiple custodians. Serevin gains a lawful response without unilateral authority over Orison’s fate.
clues.discovery: Developed while the hall distinguishes recall, emergency suspension, and measurable breach.

clues.title: Royal joinder can replace some precedent anxiety
clues.description: If Caelir joins voluntarily after seven seals are assembled, Thalan can support a broader practical settlement while denying that the court compelled every term. The king need not approve the coalition’s reasoning.
clues.discovery: Eirath states this route openly when asked what broader settlement she could support without accepting broader compulsion.

clues.title: The Crown can retain title throughout
clues.description: Thalan’s precedents confirm that the Concord places a relic in joint custody for a task; it does not alienate Crown ownership. A meaningful royal interest may remain without exclusive control.
clues.discovery: Read from the oldest surviving Concord layer beneath the hall floor.

clues.title: Necessity does not waive seasonal balance
clues.description: No emergency finding allows seven banners from fewer than four seasons to act. Thalan will not certify a moral exception to text the Chamberlain is bound to enforce.
clues.discovery: Stated at the opening of the constitutional argument and confirmed in the oldest instrument.

clues.title: Thalan precedent requires protection before compulsion
clues.description: The strongest emergency precedents compelled royal custody only after the petitioners funded substitute protection, stated an outside term, and defined an objective response to failure. Necessity authorizes the loan; it does not make Aurelune’s danger disappear.
clues.discovery: The frost record preserves three prior orders. The one lacking replacement protection was upheld only long enough to evacuate, then dissolved.

clues.title: Serevin can command the reserve while Serathiel yields the expedition
clues.description: Caldus will accept Serathiel’s troops under eastern command, allowing the marshal to support the petition without controlling the Sunseed expedition.
clues.discovery: Produced when the party separates eastern local command from command of the Orison expedition.

clues.title: A bounded ward contract
clues.description: Serevin can specify wardstone performance and duration precisely enough for Orelle to finance it as a limited contract rather than an open-ended guarantee.
clues.discovery: Produced when Serevin converts the ward package into measurable performance, duration, and delivery terms.

clues.title: The border risk strengthens the necessity finding
clues.description: Serevin’s sober assessment shows that the court is balancing two real dangers rather than giving away an idle treasure. A petition that records both risks fits Thalan’s restrained emergency theory better.
clues.discovery: Heard in Caldus’s signed assessment after ordinary movement is separated from exceptional warning signs.

clues.title: A recall panel can remain governable
clues.description: Eiral can chair a three-party recall panel requiring Serevin evidence, royal concurrence, and one expedition custodian. The arrangement answers a genuine breach without letting one house destroy the undertaking.
clues.discovery: Proposed among the lodge’s recall models after the party rejects both no response and unilateral authority.

clues.title: The six-day offer shifts risk onto Orison
clues.description: Caldus agrees that a six-day loan is safer for Aurelune and states that it leaves little margin to enter by the narrowing Crown Passage, reach the Pall's center, restore two verified dawns, and return the Sunseed. The king can truthfully call it a loan while shifting most failure risk onto Orison.
clues.discovery: Included in the lodge's explicit comparison of six-day, eight-day, and thirteen-day terms.

clues.title: Ordinary movement is not a border breach
clues.description: Several Gloam Host movements match seasonal baselines. Serevin identifies specific deviations that would justify reserve activation or recall, allowing objective triggers rather than fear-driven discretion.
clues.discovery: Established by requesting that every current report be classified as ordinary movement, warning sign, or breach evidence.

clues.title: The watch order can remain an associated instrument
clues.description: Troop deployments, ward contracts, reporting duties, and reinforcement schedules may remain in a linked security covenant. The central petition must still state what verified failure permits and who may invoke that consequence.
clues.discovery: Caldus lays the watch order beside the draft petition. Only the trigger and authority lines are copied across.

clues.title: The border watch cannot redirect the rescue
clues.description: Serevin can verify a Dawnward failure, command the eastern response, and demand the action named in the recall article without acquiring authority over Orison’s government or a different use of the Sunseed.
clues.discovery: Ask whether a border alarm could send the expedition elsewhere. Caldus answers by pointing to the undertaking line, which the watch order cannot amend.

clues.title: Eiral will protect recognition inside a broad settlement
clues.description: House Eiral can guarantee an Orison recognition compact if Ilyrion accepts neutral authorship and does not make the rescue a partisan victory over the Crown.
clues.discovery: Offered at House Eiral’s supper table as part of an eight-banner or institutionally stable settlement.

clues.title: Neutral credit can satisfy Vaudren and preserve legitimacy
clues.description: Eiral will chair the undertaking under a court-wide title and guarantee equal ceremonial precedence for Maelith and Vaudren. Neither house receives senior authorship.
clues.discovery: Heard in Eiral’s model public statement and neutral-chair arrangement.

clues.title: Royal dignity can be operative rather than decorative
clues.description: Eiral proposes royal co-custody, a joint public purpose, and language describing the act as concord after lawful disagreement. Thalan accepts these as real limits on humiliation.
clues.discovery: Set out in the operative dignity protections Theron places beside the coalition ledger.

clues.title: The succession hearing can still finish in time
clues.description: Theron can place the Ashen Bough hearing before the Masque if another public audience is shortened. The choice costs negotiation time but preserves the tenth vote as a live option.
clues.discovery: Obtained from the official calendar at the black desk; preserving it shortens another public proceeding.

clues.title: Witnessed declarations acquire political force
clues.description: At the Masque, oath-mirrors record exact words and named witnesses. A declaration remains legally short of a seal, but later withdrawal becomes a public act requiring explanation.
clues.discovery: Explained in the official Masque protocol before the party chooses its shared declaration.

clues.title: Theron must answer separately for office and house
clues.description: A direct question can require Theron to state first what the Chamberlain must certify and then what House Eiral will support. Neither answer may be used as though it were the other.
clues.discovery: Established by conducting separate official and House Eiral interviews across the apartment doorway.

clues.title: The royal counteroffer succeeds by separating private grounds
clues.description: Theron maps how Caelir can satisfy several houses individually through one royal expedition. A shared purpose and conflict mechanism force each banner to choose between the coalition’s undertaking and its private benefit.
clues.discovery: Shown when House Eiral tests the coalition against the expected royal offers.

clues.title: Eiral’s docket makes parallel bargains governable
clues.description: Theron’s office can index recognition, surety, finance, credit, and deployment covenants beside one central petition, assign review, and expose contradictions without merging every bargain into the Crown instrument.
clues.discovery: The official docket has one white page for the petition and tabbed leaves for associated instruments; each tab carries a cross-reference and a responsible reader.

clues.title: A temporary regency can satisfy Maelith
clues.description: Maelith will recognize Lady Mirath as military regent for the undertaking without deciding final inheritance. The office supplies a named noble guarantor and a lawful banner-holder.
clues.discovery: Offered in Maelith’s submission supporting a regency that ends with the Sunseed undertaking.

clues.title: Mirath will seal a credible military petition
clues.description: Lady Mirath promises the Ashen Bough to a petition with coherent expedition command and real eastern defense. She favors Serathiel’s program but can accept divided command.
clues.discovery: Stated during Mirath’s public examination and attached to the exact command structure she accepts.

clues.title: A bounded regency avoids deciding inheritance by crisis
clues.description: Thalan will support a regency ending after the Sunseed returns, with the ultimate succession reserved for later judgment. The tenth vote becomes usable without turning emergency procedure into permanent inheritance law.
clues.discovery: Set out in Thalan’s proposed emergency order reserving final succession.

clues.title: Each claimant can be held to a stated coalition price
clues.description: The hearing may require Mirath and Aven to state the conditions under which they would seal. Their answers do not cast the banner but make later reversals politically costly.
clues.discovery: Part of the public examination when the party requires each claimant to state their coalition price.

clues.title: The Ashen Bough adds a vote but no season
clues.description: The vacant banner predates the four-season arrangement and counts only toward the total. Seating either claimant cannot supply missing Autumn or Winter support.
clues.discovery: Read from the charter before the court considers any claimant or regency.

clues.title: Aven will seal for Orison’s political equality
clues.description: Aven Tal promises the banner to a petition that names Orison as a partner and gives a mortal co-custodian real authority. He does not require Ilyrion’s full constitutional language.
clues.discovery: Read in Aven’s public examination and separable from his demand for final succession.

clues.title: A recognized remedy can strengthen rather than destabilize the concord
clues.description: Eiral can accept Mirath, Aven, or a bounded regency if the stated threshold is met, the losing claim is not branded fraudulent, and the new banner-holder joins a shared public purpose rather than serving as a purchased seventh vote.
clues.discovery: Heard in Theron’s official statement of the hearing’s lawful remedies and House Eiral’s separate political response.

clues.title: The apology can become an irreversible public fact
clues.description: If Maelith acknowledges its chosen act and Vaudren accepts beneath the oath-mirrors, both houses obtain a record strong enough to support declarations or seals without agreeing on private motive.
clues.discovery: Secured through the Masque’s witnessed challenge procedure.

clues.title: Several houses can share the indemnity
clues.description: Orelle will accept a public consortium of banner guarantors if each names a bounded share before witnesses. No single house or Orison must bear the whole liability.
clues.discovery: Proposed during the Masque’s public subscription round.

clues.title: The border package can be made politically durable
clues.description: Serathiel, Orelle, and allied representatives can publicly pledge troops, wards, and funds. Serevin may then declare without waiting for every procurement instrument to be executed.
clues.discovery: Produced when the party calls the relevant actors before the oath-mirrors.

clues.title: A shared purpose can turn a count into a concord
clues.description: Eiral will treat the coalition as governable if its members publicly affirm one undertaking and accept a neutral process for conflicts, even while preserving separate reasons for support.
clues.discovery: Theron offers the declaration to coalitions approaching seven seals.

clues.title: The king offers each house its own reason
clues.description: Caelir addresses each banner on the ground it has made public: evacuation for reformers, undivided command for soldiers, compensation for Orelle, and narrow precedent for conservatives. Each offer satisfies part of a true purpose while breaking joint custody.
clues.discovery: Delivered openly at the Masque.

clues.title: Side covenants can be adopted before the petition
clues.description: The Masque can witness recognition, surety, credit, financing, and border covenants as a coordinated package. Their public adoption reduces the chance that houses later claim incompatible private meanings.
clues.discovery: Secured through the Chamberlain’s associated-instrument protocol.

clues.title: Maelith can substitute a witnessed bond for personal detention
clues.description: At the Masque, named guarantors can declare a personal bond before oath-mirrors and participating banners. The public obligation gives Maelith answerable persons without fosterage or a hostage.
clues.discovery: Produced when the party stages the surety covenant as a witnessed declaration rather than a private promise.

clues.title: A royal veto can be limited to damage and redirection
clues.description: The command article can let a royal custodian stop actions that damage the Sunseed or exceed the named undertaking without granting general control over route, tactics, or Orison’s government.
clues.discovery: Produced during the command-and-custody drafting pass.

clues.title: Audit can stabilize liability and return
clues.description: Namaris will seal when the text identifies records, inspectors, valuation dates, and the act that constitutes return. The audit article can also reassure Orelle and Maelith.
clues.discovery: Heard in the Archive’s model clause and inserted during formal drafting.

clues.title: A relic-specific sunset closes the precedent
clues.description: The petition can expire upon return and bar citation outside emergencies involving permanent planar alteration, while requiring a later constitutional review. Thalan treats this as a real limit.
clues.discovery: Available during the precedent drafting pass.

clues.title: The banner-holder must be settled before the seal is filed
clues.description: The Chamber accepts an Ashen seal only from a claimant or regent seated before filing. A final banner-holder has ordinary authority; a scope-limited regent may reaffirm corrections within the authorized undertaking but cannot bind a changed undertaking or a term beyond the regency.
clues.discovery: Read in the filing rules and the regency order attached to the Ashen docket.

clues.title: Joint custody can preserve title and grant usable authority
clues.description: The model article keeps the Sunseed Crown property while naming physical custodians, use authority, royal protections, and a return duty. Exclusive ownership and exclusive possession are not required.
clues.discovery: Heard in the first complete custody draft.

clues.title: Orison can resist a change of undertaking without vetoing ordinary command
clues.description: A mortal co-custodian may refuse a proposed use outside the named purpose, while expedition command governs route and safety within that purpose. The text protects agency and avoids paralysis.
clues.discovery: Produced when Ilyrion and Serathiel clauses are reconciled.

clues.title: Recognition can survive a narrow relic petition
clues.description: Ilyrion may reaffirm if a witnessed side compact already recognizes Orison and the final petition does not contradict it. The house need not force every reform term into the Crown instrument.
clues.discovery: Heard in Ilyrion’s final reaffirmation standard.

clues.title: Shared liability can hold through the final vote
clues.description: Orelle will keep its seal if the final text preserves bounded shares, auditable losses, and a funding source for border protection. It does not require Orison to be the sole debtor.
clues.discovery: Read in Orelle’s final conditions.

clues.title: The recall article can answer a real breach without becoming unilateral
clues.description: Serevin will reaffirm a multi-party recall triggered by measurable Dawnward failure. Ordinary troop movement and political alarm do not suffice.
clues.discovery: Read aloud as the Warden’s exact final condition.

clues.title: A withdrawal keeps its author
clues.description: The final record places each vote beside the banner’s witnessed declarations. Withdrawal remains lawful, but the court preserves the abandoned promise and the new reason under the withdrawing house’s name.
clues.discovery: Built into the order of the Conclave.

clues.title: A narrow defect need not destroy the whole petition
clues.description: The Chamberlain may identify a correctable contradiction, recess the Conclave, and accept reaffirmation from affected banners. The king cannot convert every drafting flaw into permanent defeat.
clues.discovery: Available under the certified correction procedure.

clues.title: Security commitments can answer the king’s strongest objection
clues.description: Executed ward contracts, deployment orders, and objective recall language let the coalition show that lending the Sunseed creates risk without leaving Aurelune defenseless.
clues.discovery: Presented in the final record of associated instruments.

clues.title: The procession exposes a missing season
clues.description: The banners enter by season before Eiral and the Ashen Bough. The public order makes clear that an eighth unseasoned seal cannot cure a coalition missing Spring, Summer, Autumn, or Winter.
clues.discovery: Produced when the Master of Mirrors announces the Procession of Seasons or when the party asks how the final roll call will be ordered.

clues.title: Released seals may return to corrected words
clues.description: A material amendment releases seals tied to the changed article. Those banners may reaffirm the corrected exact text in the same sitting; a defect creates delay and leverage, not automatic defeat.
clues.discovery: Read when Theron classifies corrections, material amendments, and changed undertakings.

clues.title: The chamber tests side covenants for contradiction
clues.description: Recognition, surety, finance, credit, deployment, and audit covenants can remain outside the Crown instrument if they are indexed, available to the court, and consistent with the petition’s custody, command, and undertaking.
clues.discovery: Obtained from the associated-instrument docket before the party chooses a narrow or broad central petition.

clues.title: One recall article makes the security package operative
clues.description: Ward contracts and deployment covenants can remain separate, but the petition must assemble them into one operative response: measurable failure, named verifiers, reinforcement before recall, and the authority to shorten or end the undertaking.
clues.discovery: Trace the security schedules through the clause matrix. Every line terminates at the same recall article or remains merely a promise.

clues.title: Royal joinder strengthens but does not validate the petition
clues.description: After certification, Caelir may join a broad petition voluntarily. His joinder improves legitimacy and cooperation, but seven seasonally balanced seals already bind the Crown without his assent.
clues.discovery: Read in the Conclave order when the Chamberlain distinguishes certification, compulsion, and the king’s later joinder.

clues.title: Orison can accept the final undertaking without controlling every order
clues.description: Orison’s authorized representative may accept the named undertaking and retain authority over redirection and civil government while the agreed command structure governs route, safety, and execution.
clues.discovery: Produced when Orison’s representative is called after the petition is read and before certification.

clues.title: The seasonal call precedes the seal count
clues.description: Theron calls the four seasons before he counts banners. The ceremony makes the legal order audible: Spring, Summer, Autumn, and Winter must each answer before Eiral or the Ashen Bough can increase the total.
clues.discovery: Witness the opening call. A missing seasonal standard leaves a silence that an eighth seal cannot fill.
